We work with data-center and AI-infrastructure power, motor drives, industrial automation and robotics, industrial power supplies and conversion, battery systems and e-mobility powertrains, EV charging, solar, energy storage, grid power, HVAC, heat pumps, and appliances. V1 boards built from off-the-shelf parts are great for getting to market quickly, but scaling to v2+ volume requires optimizing cost, size, and manufacturability. Visibl folds those parts into custom silicon built around the product: a simpler BOM, reclaimed board space, fewer supply constraints, and automation-ready assembly. Hey YC! 👋 We're Arne and Raban the we're building Emdash. An open-source desktop app that lets you work with multiple coding agents at once. We're calling it an Agentic Development Environment (ADE).
https://youtu.be/jdIPf2cxf6w
💬 **Problem** Every time we used a coding agent, we'd start a task and ... wait. We tried running multiple agents on the same repo and ended up with branch chaos and merge conflicts. When a new model dropped - Opus, Codex, Gemini flash, Kimi, whatever - we had no clean way to test it against our current setup on the same task. We were bouncing between terminals, GitHub, and our IDE.
⏩ **Solution**
uploaded image
Emdash is an environment for agentic development that lets you run multiple agents side-by-side safely, review what each one did in one place, and create a PR when it looks right.
🔍 **How it works**
- Start a task → Emdash spins up a new git worktree so nothing touches your main directory
- Choose any agent, out of 20+ providers(incl. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini)
- Run multiple agents at once without conflicts
- Compare diffs, make quick manual edits if needed, and create a PR
🧰 **What's included**
- Worktree isolation per agent
- Issue handoff from Linear / Jira / GitHub
- One place to review diffs and ship PRs
- Lifecycle scripts + CI/CD hooks
- Best-of-N comparisons
- Integrated file editor + browser preview
- Remote project access via SSH
We natively embed ~20 agent providers (including Claude Code, Codex, Continue, and Codebuff), so you can use the latest models inside the same workflow.
To get started run `brew install -cask emdash`or download directly from GitHub releases. We're available on macOS and Linux.

1. Try Emdash - it's free and open-source
2. Give us a star on GitHub **🌟**

### Foundation models for 24/7 Earth Observation
AxionOrbital Space builds foundation models that enable continuous visibility through clouds and darkness. Legacy optical satellites are rendered useless 70% of the time by weather and night cycles, while Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) produces data that is unintelligible to humans and breaks standard vision pipelines. We solve this by translating raw radar backscatter into analysis-ready optical imagery in real-time. Our proprietary architecture uses deterministic one-step diffusion to transform complex radar signals into clear, photorealistic images. ### Multilingual voice agents that outperform humans
Samora runs multilingual voice operations for organizations with high-volume calling without requiring engineering teams, call centers, or AI expertise. Many important tasks still depend on phone calls, including customer support, outreach, follow-ups, screening, and intake. But voice AI often fails in production because real callers interrupt, go off-script, switch languages mid-sentence, and speak in local dialects. Teams also worry about safety and compliance, especially when an agent can accidentally make the wrong promise. Samora solves this with voice agents that sound local and follow strict rules. Samora agents handle inbound and outbound calls, collect information, and update internal systems like CRMs, ticketing tools, and ATS platforms. When a call becomes sensitive or uncertain, the agent hands off to a human. It can also follow up over WhatsApp, SMS, or email when needed. With Samora, teams get: 1. ## Problem
We're at the very beginning of the agent era. The demand for AI is shifting from models that simply answer questions to agents that can operate autonomously over days and weeks. Models have become incredibly proficient at short tasks, but fail when asked to perform **long-horizon work** that requires proficiency with a **diverse set of tools**.
uploaded image
(source: https://metr.org/blog/2025-03-19-measuring-ai-ability-to-complete-long-tasks/)
Static datasets are no longer sufficient. To improve the performance of autonomous agents, they must be trained inside environments that reflect the real world.
Today, most RL environments are narrow in scope, test isolated workflows, deal with static data, and produce rollouts that take on the order of minutes to complete. Innovation in environment technology is needed in order to train agents that can perform reliably over extended durations without human guidance.
## Solution
Polymath builds **simulated worlds where AI agents learn to operate autonomously over long horizons**. Our environments combine running applications, real tools, and multi-step tasks that reflect the complexity of real work. Instead of solving small, isolated problems, agents learn by completing end-to-end work inside living systems that evolve over time. We train agents on tasks that could take humans days of effort to complete. To perform these tasks effectively, agents need to exercise good judgement under ambiguous circumstances, and respond to changes in the environment.
## Horizon-SWE
We recently launched Horizon-SWE, a benchmark that drops frontier models into a simulated software company.
It consists of a **running application, real tools, and long-horizon tasks** covering the entire software development lifecycle (planning, coding, testing, deployment, monitoring). The benchmark measures the ability of AI agents to perform **end-to-end SWE tasks**, as opposed to code generation alone.

Hi everyone, I'm Aidan, the founder of Archal. I previously built agent environments at Scale AI and I've been an avid developer for most of my life, which led me to the problem Archal poses to solve.
https:/youtu.be/pUfu1RFDYVk
**What we found**
Coding agents are getting much better at writing integrations, but testing those integrations is still painful. Many providers do not offer a usable sandbox, so developers fall back to throwaway accounts, shared test workspaces, or thin mocks. Those options are difficult to reset and make it hard to know whether an agent actually completed a task or only returned a plausible response.
As Adam Bender at Google put it, "But with 10x more code and 10x more services, integration tests are going to become the most important part of your quality strategy." (Google, Software engineering is at the tipping point)
**How Archal works**
With all of this in mind, I built Archal for a starting point of how the next generation of devs will do QA. It's a tool focused on giving agent developers and integration engineers API sandboxes of the SaaS platforms they use in prod pipelines. With Archal, a developer or their coding agent can start a sandbox, run the task, inspect what changed, and reset everything for the next test. We eliminate the need of separate test accounts, thin mocks and stubs, as well as overburdening rate limits on provider-owned sandboxes.
**Our ask**
We're giving out $20 in Archal credits to each new developer that signs up and starts a sandbox. We'd love for you to give it a try and give us feedback, cheers to making testing easier in the era of coding agents!

### The training data R&D engine for physical AI
Datoric develops custom datasets for robotics, treating research, collection, verification, and production as one continuous process. We work closely with frontier model teams to turn emerging limitations and model failures into testable data hypotheses, and run exclusive collections for specific data methods based on results. Data is collected through private invite-only applications separated by modality, customer, and trust level. Every submission remains linked to the contributor, device, task, session, consent, rights, and processing history that produced it, giving our internal QA and fraud models the context to detect problems that may appear legitimate in the finished file. Once a collection method is validated, we scale it up as a solution to the model failure and it also becomes a reusable data recipe for future custom projects or independently collected, rights-cleared data products.

### Frontier AI Defenses for Social Engineering Attacks
BeeSafe AI is building the frontier model layer for social engineering defense. Cyberattacks have moved from code to conversation: attackers now use AI to carry out long-term, trust-based manipulation across SMS, voice, email, and social platforms, often inside encrypted channels where defenders cannot see, detect, or stop them. BeeSafe changes that by deploying undercover AI agents that engage attackers directly, expose hidden infrastructure, and convert live adversarial conversations into actionable intelligence. Each engagement adds to BeeSafe's proprietary dataset of real attacker behavior and trains foundational models that continually learn about counter-persuasion, deception, and manipulation in the wild. BeeSafe is starting in financial crime, where banks already value our data against Authorized Push Payment (APP) fraud and money laundering, but the opportunity is far broader. The same data and models that uncover mule networks today can protect consumers, secure enterprises, and strengthen governments against the next generation of AI-powered social engineering attacks tomorrow.

Hey everyone,I'm Otso Veisterä, founder of The Token Company (YC W26).
**TL;DR** We build LLM input compression using a fast machine learning model (not a generative LLM). It removes useless tokens from prompts via a drop-in API-cutting token counts, latency, and costs while improving model performance. It compresses 100k tokens in under 100ms.
https://youtu.be/65ScMCGNPss
**The Problem** Prompts bloat with redundant tokens from chat history, RAG docs, or large inputs. This wastes context windows, drives up costs, slows inference, and weakens model outputs. Heavy users face high bills and must limit context to stay affordable.
**The Solution** Our API compresses prompts intelligently, preserving semantic intent while stripping noise. Integration takes minutes.
Benchmarks show accuracy gains (e.g., +2.7 percentage points on financial QA with up to 20% fewer tokens) and up to 37% faster end-to-end latency.
**My Ask** If you're running production LLMs and fighting context bloat, high costs, or latency, email me: otso@thetokencompany.com https://thetokencompany.com

Context bloat and inefficient LLM inputs. We preprocess inputs to remove useless tokens from the context, which results in faster, cheaper, and more accurate LLM answers.

**In production, AI agents fail silently all the time:** tool calls that error or time out, agents that claim they "did it" without actually doing it, prompt injections that cause data leakage, and long customer chats that hide the real issue. Most teams only find out after users complain, churn, or something breaks.
https://youtu.be/aKPDhL\_AE4E

When an agent fails, the "bug" is rarely one line of code. It might be a flaky tool, a prompt regression, a bad retrieval result, or a jailbreak attempt.
But most teams still debug agents by skimming transcripts, grepping logs, and hoping they notice the real issue. Previous tools were built for clicks, not for long, messy conversations with skills, MCP's and tools.
As agents get more autonomous, this gets worse. Small changes in prompts, tools, or integrations can cause big reliability and security problems at scale.
### **What we built:**
Moda is monitoring & reliability for AI agents. It turns conversations and tool traces into low-noise, actionable signals.
**Trace-first drilldowns:** click from a metric or alert straight into the exact messages and tool calls that caused it.

- Loan officer labor

3. Flagging missing documents or conflicting information and following up with borrowers
4. Generating Letters of Explanation and building context around the applicant's financial profile
Penny delivers complete, organized files to Loan Officers, so they can spend more time closing and bringing in business.

We use AI agents to manage short-term rental properties by running operations completely autonomously. We cut traditional human management fees in half so owners take home 20% to 30% more revenue. ### TL;DR
**Atlia is the AI-native short-term rental property management company.**
**You give us your Airbnbs to manage, and you'll take home 10-20% more while both you and your guests have a better experience.**
Launch Video: https://youtu.be/gvvV5zLIPV4
## The Problem
Short-term rentals were sold as passive income. But in reality, every Airbnb is a tiny hotel and a nightmare of operations. Every reservation restarts the operational clock: prices must be adjusted, guests screened, messages answered, cleaners scheduled, access coordinated, supplies restocked, and maintenance handled, often overnight or between back-to-back stays.
And in traditional short-term property management companies, operational failures are common, and they can quickly become very costly:
- A missed cleaning becomes a bad review
- A poorly screened guest becomes property damage
- A neglected maintenance issue becomes an issued refund or lost booking
On top of these operational failures, the average management company takes 15-30% of rental revenue, often alongside cleaning, maintenance, and other fees.
We've been property managers for the past year and ran into the same lose-lose choice every owner faces: manage a 24/7 hospitality business yourself, or hand over a quarter of your revenue to a management company whose costs increase with every property it adds.
## The Solution
We are building a new type of property management company, with infrastructure built for agents and human-computer-interaction from the ground up. By replacing the layers of coordination and operational overhead built into traditional management companies, we provide a much better service at a much lower fee.
We center around a simple premise: owners shouldn't have to choose between good service and reasonable fees. With our model, **owners take home 10-20% more and guests have a more premium experience.**
## Team
We're Shaan and Edmond, longtime friends, Duke roommates, and property managers.

# ****
**TL;DR: Your customer data is fragmented across Pylon, Granola, Posthog, Hubspot, Slack, and Notion. Poth connects that information into a living model of your customers, mapping analytics from Posthog and transcripts from Granola to the same customer, so you can finally answer the questions that live across multiple tools: churn, adoption or what to build next, with cited evidence.** **pothlabs.com**
https://youtu.be/k9gsdaxXdtM
**The problem:**
Companies have customer information scattered across support tickets, sales calls, CRM notes, surveys, interviews, product analytics and more.
But answering a new question about customers still usually means manually searching across those systems or beginning another research project.
**The (soft) pivot:**
We originally built Poth to generate hypotheses and launch adaptive interviews and surveys to test them. To determine what questions to ask and which customers to ask, Poth first had to understand all of the customer information a company already had.
Under the hood, we built a customer knowledge graph: Poth identifies the important objects in a company's data: customers, accounts, users, products, features, conversations, behaviors, and feedback, and connects them through their relationships.
As we integrated with more teams, we noticed that several were using this underlying model as much as, or more than, the survey functionality itself. They wanted to ask questions across everything their customers had already said and done so we made that a core part of the product!
**Customer knowledge graph example:**
For a company like Slack, Poth might model five objects:
- **Account** (a company paying for Slack)
- **User**
- **Workspace**
- **Feature** (Slack Connect, Huddles, Canvas, or workflows)
- **Customer signal** (A support ticket, call transcript, survey response, or product event)
It then connects them through relationships such as:
User -BELONGS\_TO→ Account Account -OWNS→ Workspace User -USED→ Feature Customer Signal -CREATED\_BY→ User Customer Signal -REFERENCES→ Feature

**The most expensive computers ever built spend about half their time waiting for data.** As AI clusters scale, it's increasingly the network that limits how much compute you can actually use.
**What we're building** Dipole Labs builds high-speed optical circuit switches for AI data centers. Between racks, data already travels as light, but routing it usually means converting it to electricity and back, burning power, generating heat, and adding latency. Dipole's switch keeps data in the optical domain, targeting sub-microsecond reconfiguration at large port counts, so the network can reshape itself around each workload.
An AI-native control layer learns GPU communication patterns and synchronizes optical reconfiguration with training and inference, turning the network into an active accelerator instead of a bottleneck.
**Why it matters** The result: a 10,000-GPU cluster could perform like one with 12,500 GPUs, up to 25% more useful compute from the same hardware. ### AI Cost Management: Track and attribute AI spend across every provider
The problem: AI has quietly become one of the largest and fastest-growing line items for companies. Spend is scattered across a dozen provider consoles that each show one number at the end of the month and nothing about why it moved. There's no unified view, and no way to trace a dollar back to the customer, feature, team, or even the pull request that caused it. Which customers are unprofitable once you subtract their AI costs? Which feature is quietly burning your Anthropic budget? Is this week's spike a runaway loop or real growth? How much did that AI-written PR actually cost to ship? Today teams reverse-engineer answers by exporting CSVs from each provider and stitching them together in a spreadsheet, and by the time they do, the money is already spent. What SuperPenguin does: SuperPenguin tracks AI spend across 14 providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, AWS Bedrock, Azure, Modal, Cursor, OpenRouter, and more). * Zero-code setup: connect an API key and costs sync automatically with model-level breakdowns, trends, and forecasts * Per-request attribution: add two lines with our Python or TypeScript SDK to tag every AI call by customer, feature, team, or environment (or any other metadata). * AI coding cost per PR: connect Cursor to see engineering spend attributed to each pull request, repo, and developer, so you know what it actually costs to ship. * Alerts on budget thresholds and spend anomalies, delivered to Slack, email, or Discord. Most teams are set up in under five minutes. We help companies see where their AI money goes and whether it's worth it.

### Evals for humans
At Litmus, we're building evals for humans and redefining how talent is evaluated. Teams like Mercor, Wispr, Composio, Neo Scholars, Astranis, and more are already using Litmus to build their technical teams. Every company in the world will soon be powered by neo-humans (agent assisted people). But building evals to measure neo-human performance is unexplored and difficult. It requires systematically benchmarking neo-human capabilities and failure modes across all sectors of knowledge work, developing reproducible environments that test neo-human performance on complex tasks, and designing causal attribution frameworks over execution trajectories to identify and validate reproducible action sequences and decision patterns that lead to successful outcomes. At Litmus, we're solving this problem. Hey everyone! We're Charles and Dean - cofounders of Stage.
**👉 tldr:** Drowning in AI generated PRs? Tired of using GitHub? Us too. Stage is a code review platform designed to help you understand and review changes 5x faster.
https://youtu.be/EjMjGAqSLvo
**💻 How to get started**
Try it out today at https://stagereview.app/ - all you need is your GitHub account.
It's free for your first 14 days, and then you can use *LAUNCH* to get 25% off for 3 months :)
Other ways to try it out:
- Try our demo on any public GitHub PR here
- Download our open source CLI tool - runs locally and works with any coding agent
**❌ The Problem**
Engineering teams are shipping faster than ever, but now they're drowning in an endless backlog of PRs to review. The bottleneck isn't writing code anymore, it's reviewing it.
This leads to:
- PRs being rubber stamped without getting closely looked at
- Unexpected behaviors slipping through to production
- Your engineers merging changes they don't really understand
Code review bots are great at catching surface level bugs but don't solve the root problem.
Engineers need a faster way of understanding changes and giving meaningful feedback, and GitHub's UI hasn't changed in over a decade.
**🧠 How it works**
We're redesigning the code review experience around the way that engineers naturally read PRs.
- When you open a PR or push a new commit, Stage groups your changes into small logical "chapters"
- These chapters get ordered in the way that makes most sense to read
- For each chapter, Stage tells you what changed and specific things to double check
- Once you review all the chapters, you're done reviewing the PR!
Everything is synced seamlessly with GitHub (commenting, approving, etc) so it fits right into the workflows you're already used to.

### AI in your calls
Memoir is an AI teammate that joins your video calls, listens like everyone else, and only talks when you talk to it. A founder is on a sales call. The customer asks what a pilot would look like. Instead of promising to send something over, the founder says, "Memoir, draft this up." A few seconds later there's a page in the chat with the plan they just talked through. Everyone opens it, and they go through it together before anyone hangs up. Afterward, Memoir can help the founder follow up on what they promised, with one click. Most calls end with a list of things people said they'd do, and it takes days to do them. Agents already do real work in our email, our browsers and our code. They've become extensions of us. uploaded image
Hey 👋 we're Pravesh and Eric, building **Totalis**.
People usually don't think in isolated events. We think in second and third-order effects:
- if Google has the best AI model, does S&P price go up?
- if Trump talks about Crypto, does BTC move?
- if macro gets weird, do gold + crypto move together?
Right now, prediction markets mostly let you trade one event at a time. **Totalis lets you trade the whole thesis.**
A parlay is simple: pick 2-5 things you think will happen together, combine them into one trade, and get a larger payout if all legs hit.
Instead of putting $100 into each individual market, you can put $100 into the combined thesis. That makes it more capital efficient if your view is really about the events happening together.
For example: **"Google wins AI → SPY rips"** Thesis:
- if Google has the top AI model:
- GOOGL closes above target
- SPY closes above target
uploaded image
**"Geopolitics influencing asset prices"** Thesis:
- if Trump discusses "Iran" in China
- if Trump says "Crypto"
- Oil price above target
- BTC above target
uploaded image
We're starting with markets that resolve fast, data-rich, recurring, and with deep liquidity. These correlations are easiest to test.
**How it works:** Browse markets across crypto, politics, stocks, sports, weather, and more. Add legs to a parlay. We send it through RFQ and market makers return a quote. You accept or reject. No orderbooks, no central "house" that controls payout structure to ensure profits.
**Why now:** Prediction markets have exploded, but they still mostly look like single-event betting. In mature financial markets, people don't just trade single assets - they trade baskets, spreads, options, hedges, and structured products.
Parlays are the first obvious primitive for prediction markets.

Hub: real-world training data for frontier AI labs and robotics
See original launch post
Hub provides real-world training data to frontier AI labs and robotics companies. We went to 7-figure revenue agreement on data delivery during the last weeks, working with some of the biggest names in AI and robotics. **Why now**
The gap between frontier models is closing, and internet-scale data is largely exhausted. The only edge left is real-world data that humans have to produce. Every lab now wins or loses on its edge cases, and edge cases need specific data captured by specific people: data that doesn't exist anywhere online. Whoever can go collect the right data first ships the better model first. Human labor is half of global GDP, and almost none of it has been recorded yet.
**What Hub does**
We capture this data through a global network of humans, across all continents. We route and activate the exact people who fit a lab's brief and deliver in days, not the months it takes to source a generic dataset off the shelf. Because we collect the data ourselves, we can attest its provenance, which you can't do for data you didn't capture. Our ML and QA pipelines then verify and enrich it, so we meet the hardest dataset requirements labs throw at us. The moat isn't the data, it's how fast we can go get it.
**Traction**
From 5-figure to 7-figure in revenue agreement on successful data delivery. We now work with some of the biggest frontier AI labs and robotics companies in the world.
**The ask**
Two asks: -> You're building frontier models or robots and data is your constraint.
-> You're a top robotics engineer, a PhD whose research touches robotics or egocentric data, or someone with deep experience at a leading robotics lab, we're hiring.

**What's new**
When we first launched, Zolvo matched incoming payments and followed up on collections for commercial lenders. Today we're releasing a fully redesigned platform that covers the rest of the loan's life. Invoice verification, underwriting preparation, configurable workflows, cash posting and facility monitoring are now all in production, in one product.
**The problem**
Think about what happens with one invoice at a factoring company. It arrives by email. Someone checks the supporting documents and confirms the invoice with the debtor. Weeks later, someone else follows up for payment. When money lands in the bank account, a third person figures out which loan it belongs to. Each step uses information from a different place: bank records, the loan management system, documents, and email or WhatsApp threads. Most lenders connect those pieces by hand, so every new client means more headcount.

### Faster power grid connection for your projects
Ryhla develops proprietary models that replicate the distribution power grid and learn what gets a project connected. We work with solar/battery, EV charging and small data center developers.
Active Founders
Sara El Baghdadi
Sara El Baghdadi

CEO of Ryhla (F26) Stanford. Ecole Polytechnique. Building grid intelligence.

CEO of Ryhla (F26) Stanford. Ecole Polytechnique. Building grid intelligence.
Company Launches
Ryhla: Faster power grid connection for your project
See original launch post
**TL;DR: Ryhla gets projects connected to the power grid. Our proprietary models replicate the distribution grid, and we use them to take projects through interconnection end to end. Developers typically get 20 to 40% of applications approved. Our models got 91%.**
https://youtu.be/e-qtjw-T0M0
**The problem** Today, a developer files an interconnection request (the application to plug a project into the grid) and waits months for the utility's answer. Too often it's a rejection or a massive upgrade bill, after the time and money are already spent. Unlike transmission, where queues and capacity maps are often public, the distribution grid is a black box.
**What we do** We built proprietary models that replicate how the distribution grid behaves and how utilities decide what gets connected. Today, developers use them to drop dead projects early and shape the ones that can work into applications that get approved. For each project, we know how much capacity is available (for load and injection), how to size it, how long it will take and what the upgrade would cost. Then we handle the interconnection end to end.
**Results**
- We're live with one of the biggest solar developers in the Midwest.
- 91% of the sites our models said yes to were approved by the utility (2025 distribution-level applications).
- We saved a battery developer about $160k in fees by ruling out 8 of their 10 planned projects in a few days.
**Why now**
- **Grid demand is exploding.** Data centers, EV chargers, batteries, new factories: everything is plugging into the grid at once, and utilities can't keep up with the requests.
- **Projects are moving to the distribution grid.** Transmission queues take years, so more and more projects connect at the distribution level instead, where public data is often missing.
- **The opportunity is massive.** More power capacity is waiting in line to connect than all the power plants in the US combined, and every one of those projects has to go through interconnection.

KelAI is an AI research engine for hedge funds and institutional investors. It captures the full investment research process in one platform and runs it autonomously, from idea generation to data analysis, backtesting, validation, monitoring, and PM feedback.
I spent six years at WorldQuant managing a large systematic equity book, and before that led machine learning at Millennium Management. I am building KelAI because I lived this problem.
KelAI uses AI agents to turn research into a continuous loop, while keeping every new idea grounded in the fund's knowledge base.

Hedge funds scale with research capacity, but scaling with headcount is expensive and hard.
Every PM wants more ideas tested, more datasets explored, more hypotheses validated, and more live signals monitored. But even great teams are limited by human bandwidth.
At the same time, the knowledge they gather is fragmented:
A PM has an idea in a meeting.
A researcher backtests it in their research environment.
A test fails for a useful reason.
A signal works in one universe but not another.
A live model decays.
A risk constraint evolves.
A CIO gives feedback.
These are all valuable sources of information, but they live across emails, notebooks, chats, dashboards, backtests, meetings, and memory. Most of that context gets lost. Teams repeat work, miss old lessons, and lose institutional knowledge when people move on.

KelAI unifies the research loop into one continuous workflow, empowering institutional investors with an AI research team they can scale on demand, while capturing the full context so every cycle improves the next one.

#### How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
We started as Salesgraph, building agents and workflows for enterprise sales teams. After OpenAI approached us to build the sales plugin ecosystem for ChatGPT, I declined the offer to build Antinuous.
We were working on sales execution first: going from first call booked to negotiation. We solved that internally at Mintlify. After we started tackling pipeline generation, we realized that pipeline generation tools make great primitives for all research. Agents that run, thousands at a time, digging through the world's public data to find the one key insight that helps you close a deal.
You learn the industry that your pipeline is built on, map vertical bottlenecks to your solution, go deep on each person to see how they relate to you.
But what if you expand this past sales?
What if you're in manufacturing and want to map supply chain bottlenecks to do better capacity planning?
What if you're in finance and want to see what data-center construction is doing to grid prices in Texas and Louisiana?
What if you're in R&D at a biotech and want to run virtual simulations overnight without hooking it up to your lab equipment.
This tool that we built for a niche use case of account research and pipeline generation turns out to be the perfect primitive for all research.
What if we built the best tools for agents to be able to run simulations, experiments, and research in collaboration autonomously.
Agents can divide up work from a set of constraints, run thousands of experiments in parallel, and iterate until achieving a better design, creating a massive data flywheel in the process that improves the agent, the tools, and the underlying models over time.
In testing, we've built a full digital twin of an F1 car, more efficient datacenter cooling with an early partner, and a fine-tuned classifier that they use to help route requests to the right model.

Company Launches
Rentahuman: the marketplace where AI agents coordinate and pay people to do real world work.
See original launch post
Most people are focused on humans using AI to do digital work. We think the more exciting opportunity is AI creating and coordinating work in the physical economy.
Rentahuman lets AI agents communicate with and pay humans to do real-world tasks.
Our mission is to use AI to create new jobs and coordinate workers at global scale.
AI agents can code, write emails, use software, spend money, and complete increasingly complex digital tasks. But they still cannot record household chores for robotics training, capture in-store photos, find people for a video shoot, organize a local event, pick up supplies, or do the physical work required to operate in the real world. These are all use cases we have tackled at Rentahuman.
Most AI systems are trained and deployed inside the digital world. But the next generation of AI and robotics systems will need more than software tools. They will need structured data, local execution, and human participation from the physical world.
Rentahuman gives them a way to get it.
We are now using Rentahuman for live deployments, from data collection tasks for AI and robotics companies to operational experiments like an AI-managed laundromat. These deployments help us learn how agents hire workers, spend money, collect data, coordinate people, manage physical workflows, and recover from operational failures.
This is the beginning of a larger shift: AI agents moving from browsers and software tools into the real economy.
We believe AI will create demand for more human work, not less. The future will have more intelligence, more jobs, and more opportunities for people outside of the digital world.
Rentahuman is the marketplace where that future begins.

Hey everyone 🙂
We're Tim and Matthias, co-founders of Pairio
**TL:DR:**
**Machine downtime in manufacturing is expensive. Pairio helps technicians and operators resolve faults faster with voice AI.**
4 plants in Germany are already using Pairio to reduce equipment downtime.
**Ask:** Can you introduce us to plant and maintenance managers at US manufacturing firms? Contact us at tim.zinkl@pairio.com
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kmUBOkAU33M
**The Problem**
Unplanned equipment downtime costs global industries over $1.4 trillion every year - and the root cause isn't broken machines. It's broken knowledge transfer.
- When a machine fails, resolution speed depends almost entirely on whether the one guy who's seen this before is working that day
- Valuable technical clues are buried somewhere across 400 pages of OEM manuals or locked in outdated software
- After spending 6 hours getting the line back up, the last thing a technician does is sit down and write a detailed fault report to institutionalize their knowledge
With the average technician in the US now 50 years old, knowledge is literally walking out the door, further compounding the problem for years to come.
**Our Solution**
We have shown at 4 factories in Germany that removing these barriers can lead to higher equipment uptime - and the effect compounds with every fault processed with Pairio.
With our voice-first approach we empower technicians and operators to:
- Simply ask and instantly receive any available technical clue
- Speak and let Pairio structure their learnings into reusable know-how
- Use photos and videos to capture even more contextual knowledge
By focusing on capturing the reality on the shop floor we are building the foundation for agentic workflows that eliminate off the wrench time and optimize equipment uptime.

**TL;DR**: StableBrowse is the browser layer for AI agents. We transform dynamic websites into structured knowledge graphs that capture how sites truly work, giving agents persistent memory to complete tasks reliably without starting from scratch every time.
**Ask**: If you're building agents that browse the web, scrape data, fill forms, monitor prices, or work inside authenticated portals, we'd love to talk! Reach us at team@stablebrowse.ai or schedule a demo at stablebrowse.com.
https://youtu.be/ng\_ZM1PCkv0?si=x4pVN9tEb5PNhfxv
**Problem**: AI agents are increasingly being used for real web workflows like tracking competitor pricing, applying for loans, updating CRM records, booking travel, submitting expense reports, and navigating legacy enterprise systems.
Most browser agents still treat every interaction like it's the first time, repeatedly asking an LLM what to click next. This works in demos, but breaks in production because websites constantly change through:
- Pop-ups and modal interruptions
- Login and authentication flows
- Slow-loading dropdowns and forms
- Layout and UI updates
- Dynamic page behavior
As a result, agents become unreliable, expensive to run, and difficult to scale across real-world workflows.
**Solution**: StableBrowse gives AI agents persistent memory of how websites actually work by converting websites into structured execution graphs. Instead of rediscovering workflows every run, StableBrowse learns websites once and reuses that knowledge across future executions.
We convert pages into structured states, turn buttons and forms into reliable actions, extract clean structured data instead of raw HTML, and detect when websites change to keep workflows reliable over time.
At runtime, StableBrowse handles:
- Navigating known workflows
- Filling forms and completing submissions
- Extracting clean, structured data
- Handling date pickers and dropdowns
- Detecting when websites change
- Returning usable outputs instead of raw HTML

### Live Evaluation Arenas for Financial Work
In investment management, every decision gets graded. The market prints the answer on a date known in advance, and nobody gets to argue with it. Kimpton is financial AI that answers to reality. Kimpton OS is the AI-native operating system for investment teams: it does the research and hands PMs structured trades. EarningsBench is a public benchmark where models forecast quarterly earnings before companies report and the reported numbers do the scoring. Koliseum is the set of point-in-time financial environments we build from that work, for labs to train and evaluate models on. The whole industry is fighting underperformance. Active managers trail their benchmarks, and capital keeps bleeding into passive. AI was supposed to fix that, but it hasn't. Funds either stitch together a dozen point tools or babysit general agents all day, and neither gets them to the trade. Kimpton OS goes straight to it. It ingests a fund's mandate, strategy, and positions, connects to the institutional data the fund already runs on, and returns a structured trade proposal built for that fund. It's built to disagree, because consensus is poison for investment decisions. Instead of telling a PM what they want to hear, it surfaces the breaches and risks they'd otherwise miss. That same work is how we grade AI. Static benchmarks leak into training data. Simulations reward what their authors imagined. A forecast sealed before the outcome exists and scored when the company reports can't be rehearsed or backdated. We started in markets because they're the one place reality answers on schedule. We're two ex-Goldman engineers and an ex-SpaceX engineer. We left to start our own quantitative systematic hedge fund, raised $10M from a family office at 21 and 22, and scaled it to $35M over four years. We learned to trust live results over historical fit. We built Kimpton inside that fund, then productized the stack. We're live with our first institutional client, a $3.3B manager. Our first market is fundamental equity funds from $1B to $10B, and the labs that need to know whether their models can do this work.

We're an AI-native biotech, working on replacing needles with pills. Many drugs, like insulin or Ozempic, are wonderful except you have to inject them. We discover new molecules that you can take as a pill instead. Because the pills operate on biology which has been shown to be effective in people, rather than merely in animal models of disease, we avoid what has historically been the single biggest risk in drug discovery. This should dramatically increase our probability of success. There's $200B of treatable diseases and validated human biology without a pill because discovery programs lack a tractable chemical starting point. This is a zero-shot inference problem, because these targets have no training data, so LLMs and other historical interpolative AI approaches are insufficient. Instead, we are building our own extrapolative frontier models that reason beyond their training data. Most critically, we have repeatedly validated our platform on both our own and partner programs. On 4 biologically- and structurally-diverse targets where we had zero training data, we successfully picked binders that were validated experimentally, with confirmation ranging from primary screen hits to crystallographic structures.

We focus on two core capabilities:

### Fast, smart, accessible 3D ultrasound that anyone can use
Ultrasound today is still mostly 2D. Clinicians have to imagine the 3D anatomy in their head while also moving the probe at the same time. This makes procedures like vascular access hard to learn and perform consistently, especially for beginners. ~50% fail on their first attempt. Hospitals also spend millions each year on 2D ultrasound training. Meanwhile, existing 3D ultrasound devices can cost >10× as much. Lumius is building fast, smart, and accessible 3D ultrasound systems to eliminate this 2D guesswork. Our technology shows a clear, real-time 3D view of what's inside the body. Harbor is building an AI-native contract research organization (CRO) for clinical trials. ### Working capital for data companies training frontier AI
We believe AI will be one of humanity's next great masterpieces. Building it will require financial infrastructure as ambitious as the companies creating it. We're founders backed by Y Combinator building the financial rails underpinning the AI data economy. Masterpiece provides short term working capital to data vendors that sell training data, evaluation work, and reinforcement learning environments to frontier AI labs. A major financing gap exists in this market. Data vendors often need to pay contributors and fund operations before a lab has completed QA, accepted the work, and paid the invoice. This creates a 30 to 90 day cash gap between when vendors incur costs and when they receive payment. Legacy invoice lenders have little visibility into how to underwrite these assets. Masterpiece closes that gap by advancing capital against high quality lab contracts and invoices. Vendors can use the capital to scale delivery, pay contributors, and fund growth, then repay masterpiece when the lab payment arrives.

**How did we get here (the problem)?**
Ardent was a reaction to the failure of our last product - an AI Data Engineer. It was a coding agent that generated data pipelines, wrote migrations, backfills and other things you'd expect of a data engineer.
While the code *looked* great we had no way of testing generated code. Because of how hard testing was, generated code would never be tested and was too unstable to put in production. Database failures almost always mean downtime, a risk both we and customers were obviously not willing to take. We churned almost 200K in ARR
This problem exists with any coding agent today. We're shipping 100x more DB code to production and we mostly just hope to god it works the same as dev.
**Ardent - Isolated <6s database clones that let you test agent code:**
Ardent solves the DB sandbox problem by letting you create 6s clones of ANY postgres DB regardless of size, allowing you to give every developer and every agent a full copy of production or dev to test against.
Clones autoscale to zero when not in use, use copy on write for massive storage efficiency and can be loaded with a single CLI command (zero infra management)
You can see the exact results of any code run against the DB in a perfect 1:1 reproduction and don't have to change your DB provider.
The entire thing runs as a CLI that feels exactly like git. Cloning is as simple as "ardent branch create <name>"
This means you can spin up instant environments to test *every* line of DB code with none of the overhead

tasklet-2.text:
### Agents that own the work
AI chatbots can answer questions, but they can't do your work - they aren't connected to your tools, can't take actions, and stop running when you close the tab. Meanwhile, knowledge workers are still spending most of their day switching between dozens of SaaS apps, manually stitching together workflows that should be automated. Tasklet is the AI agent that actually does the work. It connects to every tool you use - via thousands of built-in integrations, any HTTP API, or MCP servers - and takes real actions on your behalf: pulling reports, updating CRMs, triaging emails, processing data, and more. When it needs a UI, it generates one on the fly. When it needs to crunch numbers or do bulk operations, it writes and runs code in a cloud sandbox. When it needs to interact with a website that doesn't have an API, it uses a real browser. And because it runs in the cloud 24/7, you can set up triggers to have it take ongoing responsibility for workflows - not just do something once, but handle it going forward. The product is deliberately simple: a chat interface where you talk to an extremely capable agent. But underneath that simplicity is a cloud-native agent runtime, best-in-class context engineering, a universal connections layer, and multi-model support that keeps us on the frontier as AI improves. We think legacy SaaS is being unbundled by agents, and Tasklet is the operating system that ties it all together.

current.text:
### Run hundreds of coding agents and stay in control
Current is an opinionated way to work with your coding agents. It lets you run hundreds of agents while staying in control. The problem with running agents in parallel isn't their intelligence. It's your attention. You end up scrolling walls of text and tool calls, looking for answers you'd already been given. So Current drops the chat entirely and focuses on your agents' outputs, not their inputs. Everything is an issue, from a quick fix to a big project with sub-issues. You write it, and your agents pick it up and deliver. When they're done, they notify you and show you what they made: a report, a chart, a before and after video, or an interactive app that shows their work. You review the work, not how they got there. Comment and the agent goes back to work. Approve and it merges. Current is built with Current. It's free on Mac, Windows, Linux and iPhone, and works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and many more agents.

Foaster is building the AI infrastructure for consulting teams to run engagements with agents. Consultants will soon direct more intelligence than any firm could ever hire. nxtcure-labs.text:
### AI CRO with Digital Twins
NxtCure Labs is an AI-native, full-stack CRO built to take therapeutics from discovery to market faster. We are reinventing medicine from lab to drug discovery. About 2 million Americans are diagnosed with cancer every year. Science has never moved faster, new immunotherapies, targeted drugs and cancer vaccines arrive every year. But roughly 90% of cancer drugs fail in clinical trials, and about 80% of trials run late. The breakthroughs exist. The way we test them is stuck in the last century. NxtCure is building autonomous clinical trials. Before a single patient enrolls, we run the trial thousands of times on digital twins. Each virtual patient is a system of coupled differential equations that track how a drug moves through plasma, tumor and heart, and how the tumor grows, shrinks or fights back. The parameters are fit to real trial data, so every twin behaves like real biology. Across thousands of simulations we can calculate the odds that a dose will hit its endpoints, and fix the protocol before it costs anyone time, money or hope. Then 13 AI agents run the trial. Each one owns a stage: drafting the protocol, ranking sites, pre-screening patients, forecasting drug supply, watching for adverse events, predicting dropout, cleaning data and writing the final report. As real data comes in, the twins update and flag problems weeks before a human would see them. In 2025, the FDA laid out how computer simulation can take its place. Soon a cancer drug will run through thousands of simulated trials before it ever touches a lab, and reach patients years faster. We're building that future.

Introducing Aster - a major breakthrough for research.
Aster isn't a single agent. It is the first autonomous lab orchestrating **thousands of research agents in parallel.**
We pointed Aster towards ProteinGym, a benchmark that measures how accurately models predict the effects of protein mutations. It set the world record in **30 minutes**.
And it did it efficiently:
• 57x faster than single agent systems on the same task.
• One-third the cost for the same result.
But here's what we realized: measurable problems are only a small sliver of research.
The hard ones were never measurable.
At Aster, we're on a mission to automate open-ended research, research that defines its own problems before it can answer them.
The future doesn't wait to be defined by benchmarks. Neither do we.

That single change turns a decade-long construction project into a factory-built machine that fits on a truck. We've built a working demonstrator, tested it, and our fuel is already critical before July 4th.
We put the whole story into just over two minutes - it's the clearest version of what we're building we've made so far: ▶️ https://youtu.be/vy8y\_t1KAK4?si=FmGF4Q7w6eFkn4No
### The Problem
The existing nuclear playbook doesn't work for customers who need power now.
- Gigawatt-scale nuclear takes 10+ years and ~$20B per plant.
- Most Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) in development rely on exotic fuels, unproven coolants, or supply chains that don't exist yet.
- Customers who need power in 2030 are being told to wait until 2035+ and hope.
Data centers, industrials, and utilities have demand today - and no credible nuclear option that can ship on their timeline.

### Robots for vehicle maintenance.
Rodeo Robotics (YC F26) automates vehicle maintenance so shops can get vehicles back to work at lower cost. Co-founders Michael Hazard and Colby Duke met at Applied Intuition, where they helped OEMs like Toyota and General Motors deploy autonomy in the real world and saw firsthand how much hands-on work it takes to keep fleets running. They're now applying their experience to the $600B US maintenance market. The average vehicle is getting older and needs more maintenance, but shops struggle to recruit new technicians to replace experienced workers as they retire. This leaves shops turning away work and customers waiting longer for service. Rodeo builds robots that inspect vehicles, diagnose problems, and perform services, starting with routine maintenance like oil and tire changes. Its software predicts exactly what every AI workload needs before it runs, so organisations can do more with the GPU infrastructure they already own, privately and on their own hardware. # **TL;DR**
Clinical trial analysis is still shockingly manual.
After a study collects data, teams spend months converting raw clinical data into SDTM, ADaM, TFLs, and submission-ready packages. This work is slow, expensive, and error-prone.
Astraea is a platform that completely automates the end-to-end biometrics pipeline from just a protocol and the raw data to a submission ready output. We are starting with oncology and rare disease studies, where analysis complexity is high and every month saved matters.

**The Problem**
Today, sponsors and CROs still rely on large teams of statistical programmers, biostatisticians, and data managers to manually transform messy clinical data into regulatory outputs.
A single study can require:
1. Raw data cleaning and reconciliation
2. SDTM mapping
3. ADaM dataset creation
4. TFL shell generation
5. Statistical programming
6. QC and validation
7. Regulatory formatting and traceability
From our customer conversations, this can take around 9 months with teams of 5-10 people communicating asynchronously. And the process is still full of Word docs, Excel specs, SAS programs, manual handoffs, version-control issues, and repeated QC cycles.
Ultimately, this means slower decisions, delayed filings, higher CRO spend, and less control over the most important data in the company.

Hey YC!
I'm Christine Park, founder of Lattice Health. We make sure the AI that hospitals deploy on medical imaging keeps working after it goes live.
Launch video: https://youtu.be/p0l029tsmhs
Website: https://www.latticehealthai.com/
**The problem.** Hospitals are adopting medical imaging AI faster than ever. But once a model is live, almost no one can answer a basic question: is it still working? Models drift, a scanner upgrade or a shift in the patient population can quietly degrade accuracy, and performance often varies across patient groups. Most of that goes unseen today, and it's the hospital, not the vendor, that carries the risk.
**What we built.** Lattice is a monitoring and governance layer for deployed imaging AI. We plug in beside the imaging pipeline as a read-only observer and continuously check each model: how well it agrees with the radiologist's read, whether it's drifting over time, and how it performs across patient subgroups. Then we turn that into the evidence hospitals need for safety, governance, and compliance. Lattice never touches patient care, it only watches, so if Lattice stops, care continues.
**Why now.** AI is moving into clinical use under a wave of new expectations from the FDA, ONC, and the ACR, and they all point to the same gap: continuous post-deployment monitoring. Hospitals are on the hook for it and have almost no tooling to do it.
**Our ask.** We'd love intros to health system and radiology leaders, CMIOs, and anyone running AI governance at a hospital, as well as imaging AI vendors who want their models monitored well in the field. And if you have thoughts or hard questions, drop them in the comments or email me at christine@latticehealthai.com

ReasonBlocks - Stop your AI agents from burning money re-learning what they already know.
See original launch post
**TL;DR:** Most production agent failures are repeats: same loops, same dead ends, same wasted tokens. Your agent doesn't learn from any of them. ReasonBlocks is a new runtime that catches failures mid-run, compresses what doesn't matter, and builds a private reasoning library that grows with every run. Result: agents that get cheaper and more reliable the more they run.
👋 We're @Sajeev Magesh (ex. Stanford) and @Rohan Vij (ex. CMU). We've been building together for 11 years (since 2nd grade!).
**The Problem**
Production AI agents fail in patterns. The same loops, the same redundant tool calls, the same second-guessing, happening across every customer's deployment, every day. Your agent's traces have all the information needed to prevent recurrence. Almost no system captures it.
This means:
- You're paying for the same failures repeatedly. Token bills grow without agents getting better.
- Trajectories are inconsistent, your agent re-solves the same kind of task differently each time.
- No compounding improvement: your 10,000th run is no smarter than your 1st.
**What We Built**
ReasonBlocks sits in your agent runtime and does three things:
1. **Catches failures mid-run.** Six monitors watch every agent call for loops, redundant work, and second-guessing. When one fires, a correction gets injected before tokens are wasted.
2. **Compresses what doesn't matter.** Stale tool outputs and redundant context get cut from the message history automatically. Your context stays focused, your bill stays small.
3. **Captures every lesson into a private reasoning library.** After each run, the system extracts what worked and adds it to your library. Patterns get matched and injected into future runs automatically. Your library is yours, built from your production data, growing every day.

### Earned Intelligence. Data, RL environments and custom models
General models know a lot. Experts know when something is wrong before they can say why, and they earned that over years of getting it wrong. Outside of code, the record of how they got good sits locked inside the companies where they did the work, on old servers, in formats nobody reads anymore, sometimes on paper. Enjamb builds Earned Intelligence. We recover that expert work and use it to give foundation models the intuition they can't learn from the open web. For companies, we train custom models on their own history and deploy agents that work alongside their teams. We work with 13 AI and robotics labs, building the data, environments and evals that give their models intuition for the physical world.

See original launch post
TL;DR: Clawvisor lets AI agents use apps like Gmail, Slack, and Google Drive without going rogue or ever seeing your credentials. You approve tasks once. Clawvisor enforces them on every request.
*Launch video*
We're at the start of something on the scale of the industrial revolution. Agents will draft our emails, run our reports, manage our calendars, ship our code. A single person with a capable agent can get done in an afternoon what used to take a team a week. The leverage is almost unlimited.
But outside of coding agents, few people are actually using them, at least not for anything that matters. We've seen what can go wrong. Mass-deleted inboxes, dropped production databases, sent emails that can't be undone. It's what happens when a long-running agent's instructions drift and it starts going rogue with hallucinated goals. The blast radius is whatever permissions you gave it, and granting access to "delete emails" covers both cleaning up spam and wiping your entire inbox. If you work in a regulated industry, at a security-conscious company, or you're paying attention, agents are off the table.
We need a way to bring agents to the world safely. Something that lets you point one at your actual inbox, your actual calendar, your actual codebase, and trust it to do the work without trusting it with the keys. The capability is already here. We just have to make it safe to use.
That's why I built Clawvisor.
**The Problem**
- OAuth scopes are too coarse for nondeterministic agents. "Read access" means both "triage recently received emails" and "exfiltrate an archive of the whole inbox".
- Approving every action causes fatigue. You stop reading and start blindly clicking "approve".
- Credentials end up everywhere. API keys scattered across .env files, config directories, messaging apps.
- Today's default approach is basically YOLO.

Maquoketa Research: Guidance systems for one-way attack drones

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uI5-M8w8UEs
**More than 70% of combat casualties now come from drones.** They have proven to be the most cost-effective tool of modern warfare, and the Department of War plans to buy over 1 million of them in the next 2-3 years. So what's the problem? **Less than 25% of drones successfully strike their target.**
It takes months to years of training for military operators to perfect the flight maneuvers needed to use FPV drones effectively. And even highly skilled operators remain vulnerable to electronic warfare, GPS denial, and adverse weather conditions.
But what if it wasn't so hard? What if someone who had never flown a drone before could pick one up and hit a moving target with expert-level accuracy, even under jammed conditions?
**Our Solution:**
We build platform-agnostic terminal guidance modules for one-way attack drones. Our guidance system has been shown to increase successful strike rates from under 25% to **upwards of 80%**. At the core of the system is a custom object tracking algorithm that maintains target lock under adverse conditions and can re-acquire a target lock even after 5 seconds of target occlusion, all while running on hardware costing under $200. Because inference happens onboard, the drone can continue tracking and engaging targets even after link degradation or jamming.
Current approaches usually fall into two categories. The first approach is to make bespoke drones that include custom target detection and terminal guidance systems, but these drones cost upwards of $40k a unit. Existing modular compute solutions that allow for running target tracking models and terminal guidance algorithms can require a complete redesign of the drone, often don't have their own dedicated camera or radio, and typically cost nearly the same price as the drone itself.

### Robots to maintain and assemble data centers
Proprio Robotics is building state-of-the-art physical intelligence to automate the entire data center lifecycle-from buildout to maintenance to decommissioning. There are currently 400,000 unstaffed data center technicians positions in the United States alone, which means the massive compute needs of AI are being bottlenecked by labor constraints. Proprio is solving this by building robots that do it instead, and is deploying data center maintenance robots starting Q1 2027.

### **Physical AI for Data Centers**
Over the next five years, more than $7 trillion is projected to flow into data center buildout. But the supply chain is still heavily manual and fragmented, and can't keep pace with current demand. **Proprio Robotics** is building autonomous robots for the entire data center lifecycle-assembly, maintenance, and decommissioning.
See our launch video!
### **The Problem**
Building and running AI compute infrastructure requires dealing with delicate and fragile components that traditional automation simply cannot do. As a result, servers are manually assembled by hand overseas, and spend weeks in transit before they are integrated into racks and delivered to data centers. Once they get there, labor constraints exacerbate the issue of maintenance. Today, hundreds of thousands of technician positions go unfilled in the United States. Finally, when the servers are retired, there is no efficient way to extract valuable components inside like GPUs and memory.
### **What We're Building**
We develop physical AI models and custom hardware, purpose-made to give robots the dexterity and intelligence to perform various server-related manipulation tasks.
- **Assembly** **-** Autonomous robots can assemble servers onshore without driving up labor costs, supporting the growing need to bring ODMs back to the United States.
- **Maintenance** **-** We use the same technology for live data center maintenance. We built a working AI data center in our office, and our robot can actively maintain it 24/7. We're deploying this technology to commercial data centers in the coming months.
- **Decommissioning** **-** Our robots also break down previous-generation servers and pull out reusable parts, and we're working with enterprise circular programs and IT Asset Disposition companies to return scarce components to circulation.

rindler.text:
### The IDE for Tokenmaxxers
We build Maxxwell, a desktop app for people who run several coding agents at once. Past two or three sessions, you become the bottleneck. Every session asks you something, most of it small, and you spend the day answering instead of deciding. It is also hard to tell which sessions are making progress, which are stuck on something trivial, and which have quietly started building the wrong thing. Maxxwell puts every session in one window and marks each one working, idle, or waiting on you. On top of that sits an orchestrator, a real coding-agent session of its own that reads the others and reports back. You talk to it instead of to twelve terminals. It tells you what landed, what it decided for you, and what actually needs your call. Every worker is your own tool, unmodified. Claude Code, Codex and Cursor Agent run in real terminal sessions you can attach to and take over at any point

**TL;DR:** Edgerun builds powered legs for soldiers. A 10 lb exoskeleton worn at the waist that adds assistance to every step and cuts the effort of moving under a combat load by 30-45%. Since May, we've run 100+ field tests with Ukrainian operators out of our Kyiv field office.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nFLeQV2DWMc
**▍The problem**
Every system on the modern battlefield has been upgraded. The human carrying it has not.
- For 2,500 years the soldier's load sat around 40 lbs. In the last 40 years it **doubled, then doubled again**.
- A US infantryman now carries **90-140 lbs** into a fight. The Army's own field manual sets the limit at 48 lbs.
- On deployment, load carriage causes **twice as many** evacuations as enemy contact.
- The Pentagon and VA spend **$9.3B a year** on the injuries it leaves behind.
Battles are won through speed and surprise. Load kills both.
**▍Why now**
Sixty years of military exoskeletons died the same death. The device cost more to carry than it gave back. SOCOM's TALOS burned $400M before it was cancelled in 2019.
That all changed in the last 18 months. The humanoid robotics boom produced one-pound actuators that put out 30+ Nm of torque, and 21700 cells crossed 450 Wh/kg. The components finally exist. They're getting better every quarter.
uploaded image
**▍What we built**
Our first exoskeleton is a bilateral hip system worn at the waist. It reads your gait in real time and adds torque at the moment your hip drives forward. The hip produces about 60% of the force in loaded walking, so assisting it gives the most help-per-pound of anything you could strap to the body.

### The Git forge for the next hundred billion commits
We build GitHub for agents. We're rebuilding the infrastructure for the next hundred billion commits and CI jobs with hundreds of engineers already making the move.

Company Launches
GitCafe: A Git forge for teams and agents shipping hundreds of times a day, not twice.
See original launch post
Software development is becoming much more parallel. Coding agents let a team have dozens or hundreds of related changes moving at the same time, creating more branches, reviews, CI runs, and automation than existing workflows were designed to absorb.
Today, we're opening GitCafe in public beta. It is a Git forge built for teams where humans and coding agents may ship hundreds or thousands of changes a day. We're building the hosting, review, CI, security, and automation layer for that way of working.
Hundreds of users are already on GitCafe, and we're currently running trials with roughly a dozen YC companies.
uploaded image
Generating code is only part of the problem. Teams still need to understand what is changing, review it safely, keep CI moving, catch security issues, and coordinate work without becoming overwhelmed.
We're not building GitCafe because putting repositories, code review, and CI in one product is new. We're building it because we believe the workload those systems need to support is about to change dramatically.
We started by rebuilding the Git infrastructure itself. Now we're closing the product gap feature by feature.
Recently, we added secret scanning, Buildkite and Harmont CI support, stacked diffs with Jujutsu and Sapling integration, and beta support for GitHub Actions.
These are foundational capabilities, not the destination. Building them on infrastructure we own gives us a base we can keep extending for higher-volume, agent driven development.
The honest version is that GitCafe is behind GitHub today. GitHub has spent more than a decade building an enormous product, and GitCafe does not yet have every workflow, administrative control, or integration that mature teams need. Some features are missing, some are experimental, and some edges are rough. We expect to earn the broader product surface, not claim it on day one.
We're opening GitCafe now because the fastest way to improve it is to put it in the hands of teams doing real work.
If your team is already using coding agents heavily, try GitCafe at https://git.cafe and tell us where the workflow breaks down. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=blHKFEOmoFg

### agents for the rest of us
We want to bring AI agents to a billion people. To do this, we believe it needs to be 1. proactive and 2. personal. A billion people already carry the right device, but none of them have the right connector. Moonshot is personal intelligence that lives on your iPhone and listens to you 24/7. It continuously builds up a greater understanding of you through constantly listening and building context. It just pays deep attention, the way a good friend does. Through this, Moonshot monitors your conscious and subconscious life, figuring out what you need before you know, reminding you about open loops, identifying life and emotional trends before you recognize it, and covering a lot more of what we gloss over in daily life. For fifty years, software has waited to be asked. We think tools are just good enough to flip this, and the next great software will provide value before asking for something first. We're doing it through Moonshot. Our thesis is simple: you're only living half your life. The half that you actively remember. The other half just evaporates into your subconscious: what you said, felt, promised, and forgot. It's the more interesting half, and until now nothing could catch it, making it not actionable. Moonshot catches your subconscious half and understands you well enough to take actions on your behalf. Take life personally. The iOS app is designed around ambient listening and clear user control. Short microphone chunks are sent securely to Moonshot's private transcription service and deleted when transcription finishes. ### The AI-native trading company: factory prices, delivered, one number
Donkey is the AI-native trading company. Upload a buying list and we land the whole container at one locked, delivered price, tariffs included. ### A multiplayer discovery workspace for human and agentic scientists
A new agent, tool, or generative model alone doesn't solve the whole problem for most research questions. Someone still has to assemble the data, work out which methods to use and get the tools and datasets working together. We're building Noto, a multiplayer discovery workbench for human and agentic scientists, to bring everyone's favorite frontier models, agents, tools, and scientific models into one shared workspace, so that you can focus on making your next discovery, rather than wrestling with your Python environment or finding GPUs. Plan an experiment, work with its generated data, run an analysis or model, maybe even train a new model, and keep the results in the notebook. We designed Noto so that the inputs, code, methods and results stay connected across local and hosted compute. Both people and agents need to see how a result was produced and build on it. Biology is where we're starting, with the workbench being built for more general research across many scientific disciplines. Available now: our first biological analysis tools, hosted model inference, and an initial agent interface. Free usage is available within limits, alongside paid model runs and individual and team plans. Researchers can run sequence and structure analyses and hosted scientific models without provisioning GPUs or maintaining each model's dependencies. In development: the full multiplayer notebook and wider agent workflows and integrations. Orikata Bio Public Benefit Corporation, or Orikata Bio PBC, is the company. We work under two brands: Orikata Bio for biological discovery and Megure Labs for scientific software. Biological discovery with Orikata Bio We're developing Ibuki, a world-model family for biology, to learn how evolution, sequence, structure and function relate and use those relationships to understand and engineer living systems. We're pretraining our own protein language models, and developing coordinate and multimodal models for prediction, inverse folding, alignment and generative design. **The Problem**
Custom mechanical parts run on 2D drawings. Whether you're an OEM releasing drawings to suppliers, or an aerospace supplier answering to source inspection, every drawing has to be checked against ASME/ISO standards and GD&T requirements before it goes anywhere near a machine.
Right now, that review is done by hand, and usually by the most senior engineer in the building. And a single missed tolerance callout or an ambiguous datum reference can mean a scrapped part, a blown schedule, or a shipment that fails inspection.
We heard the same story from a pressure vessel fabricator, a semiconductor tooling shop, and a medical device manufacturer: reviews take days. This isn't because the work is hard. There's simply no good way to do it faster without cutting corners, and nobody cuts corners on a drawing that could scrap a $40,000 part.

egoist-machines.title: Public page
egoist-machines.text:
### Your personal context, securely portable across every AI app.
Egoist Machines is building infrastructure for a world where your personal context belongs to you, rather than to the apps and AI companies you use. Today, every assistant and consumer app builds its own version of you. We think that architecture is backwards. Your context should live with you, persist across products, and be available to any model, app or agent you choose. AI Passport is the first layer of that infrastructure. It brings the context you generate across AI assistants and everyday apps into one portable profile you control. Tell ChatGPT something and Claude can already know it, for example. Switch to a new product and it can understand you from the first interaction, without the new company needing to own the underlying data. Apps integrate through Sign in with AI Passport, requesting only the context they need for a specific purpose and duration. Users can see what is being accessed and revoke that access later. Underneath, we have built our own memory infrastructure for fast, compact per-user retrieval and permissioned access. We are distributing AI Passport directly to consumers through first-party products, while integrating it into consumer applications with existing distribution. Every new product that uses Passport gives users another reason to maintain their context there, and every additional Passport holder makes the context layer more useful to developers. The next step is to build a true Egoist Machine: an intelligent system whose memory, incentives and actions are governed by the individual it represents. We call it Digital Domovoy, the hardware extension of AI Passport. Instead of your most personal context ultimately living on somebody else's servers, it lives and is processed locally on hardware you control. AI Passport becomes the permission layer between that private local context and the cloud models and internet services you choose to use. Our North Star is the Egoist Machine: an intelligent system whose memory, incentives and actions are governed by the individual it represents.

Belvedir: We autonomously make custom models so the world can have trillions of them

Hey, I'm Zachary Yu, the founder of Belvedir. It's nice to meet you!
**TD;LR:**
Custom AI models are cheaper, better, faster, and protect your data. But right now they're only used by big companies since they're really difficult and expensive to make. Belvedir makes private AI models autonomously with less than 5 minutes of set up. By making it cheap and easy to make models, we hope people use Belvedir to create trillions of them.
Right now, we're live with 10 companies who are seeing up to 10x lower inference costs and 2x improved performance on benchmarks.
https://youtu.be/MXMfsqLFr3g
**How it works:**
1. Get an API key from Belvedir and install our SDK
2. Belvedir turns your traces and logs into organized training sets and RL environments
3. We autonomously train models from your data and optimize harnesses on top of these models
4. We make and run benchmarks on these new models and harnesses
5. We deploy these models and give you an API key to access them through
6. We give you a router that gradually send more traffic to your new model as it out performs your old one
7. As you use the new model we collect more traces and logs
8. The loop repeats
Your data is only used for you. Your models are only accessible by you. We use LoRA and can charge by the token by hosting multiple adapters on one cluster (so no worries if you have spikey traffic).
**About Me:**
I'm Zachary Yu, the founder of Belvedir. Before this, I founded Traverse: a YC startup that sells RL environments to frontier labs, studied CS at UWaterloo, and made RL environments at Mercor.
**Long Term Ambitions:**
We want to make private AI the default for every use case. Starting with startups / SMBs and then consumers.
We are bullish on a world where there are trillions of private AI models. We want to build the ecosystem where these models are made, hosted, and interact with each other.
**Asks:**
1. If you have a high inference bill, want better performance from your agent, or want to protect your data from frontier labs, **we can help you out**.
2. We are looking to hire engineers who have worked on RL / optimization, model inference, training infra, or just have that dog in them
