We train human brain cells for compute. In March, we trained them to play Doom; now we got them to do next-token prediction.
uploaded image
uploaded image
**The Problem**
Modern models require enormous amounts of energy and training data, while still struggling with continual learning and adapting efficiently to new tasks. Biological brains solve these problems very differently. They learn continuously, adapt from limited experience, and operate on roughly the power of a light bulb. **Solution**
Parasma is developing the algorithms and infrastructure needed to turn human brain cells into useful compute. The human brain is the most capable and energy-efficient learning system we know. Our goal is to reliably train biological substrates and use them for general computation, robotics, and eventually direct biological training. In March, we trained human brain cells to play Doom, which got hundreds of millions of views across social media. Since then, we've been working toward more general tasks. Most recently, we got the cells to perform token prediction: given a sequence of tokens converted to electrical stimuli, the neurons learn to predict what comes next with no GPU.
Long-term, biological compute will offer orders-of-magnitude improvements in energy and sample efficiency, while enabling native continual learning.

I previously worked on neuromorphic computing and reinforcement learning during my master's.
Before that, I built a successful digital-item marketplace with > $1.7M of listed goods and played games professionally.

musicarena.text:
### The crowdsourced benchmark for AI-generated music and music production
https://musicarena.io/
Company Launches
🎵 MusicArena - the arena for AI music-making 🎵
See original launch post
**Paucis verbis:**
The idea is simple: give two systems the same music task, listen to what they make, and vote for the better result.
We're starting with AI agents producing music inside a DAW.
Give two agents the same task, watch them work, listen to the finished tracks, and vote for the winner.
https://youtu.be/Lxo08Axk-YM
**Why start with LLMs?**
Most existing AI music benchmarks focus on models that generate audio end-to-end.
We think there's another category that's going to become increasingly important: general-purpose models that can hear music, reason about it, and operate the same creative tools humans use.
Frontier models are already becoming much better at computer use, and we expect audio to increasingly become a native modality as well.
Today, these agents are largely operating through tool calls/computer use rather than actually listening to their own output. But as audio becomes a native modality for frontier models, we expect agents to increasingly be able to hear the music they're making and iterate on it directly.
Music makes for an especially interesting test because there often isn't an objective answer, so human preference matters.
**WE NEED YOU!**
Pull up to our website and try it out yourself! musicarena.io
Want your model on the leaderboard? Forward us an email at founders@musicarena.io 🦁

### Real-world RL environments for robotics models
Enact creates the physical environments to benchmark and hill climb robotics models on high-value tasks. We find where robots fail, and fix them with our in-house training loop.

Company Launches
Enact: post-training infrastructure for robotics models
See original launch post
**TL;DR: Enact helps teams deploy robots that work in the real world. We roll out policies, generate failure / recovery data, and run in-house evaluations so robots can complete real tasks in production.**
**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dam0tQBIezY**
**The Problem**
Robotics models can look flawless in choreographed demos and still fail when an object slips, the scene shifts, or the robot makes an early mistake. Those failures push the policy into states its training data never taught it to recover from. **Robotics models must train on edge cases to be reliable in the real world.**
**What We Built**
Enact turns a policy's failures into targeted recovery datasets for teams training robotics models. We use the data to fine-tune models and run real-world evaluations, verifying our data improves reliability.
**We're already serving our first customers: finding where their robots fail and collecting the targeted recovery data needed to make them robust.**
- Roll out an existing model on a physical robot.
- Identify recurring failure states.
- Recreate those states and demonstrate how to recover.
- Retrain with the new trajectories added in.
- Repeat
**Targeted recovery data pushes success rates above 99%.**
On our controlled packing task using pi0.5 on the YAM 6DoF arms:
- 200 ordinary expert demonstrations: 90/100 successful physical rollouts
- 250 ordinary expert demonstrations (more of the same data): 89/100
- 200 expert demonstrations plus 50 targeted recovery demonstrations: 99/100
uploaded image
**We're continuing to longer-horizon tasks such as industrial kitting, lab automation, and electronics recycling**
Longer-horizon tasks need substantially more base and recovery data, but the loop is the same: find failures, target missing behaviors, retrain, repeat.

We're James Stevens and Govind Chada, and we met at Stanford. Govind researched real-world robot adaptation in Chelsea Finn's IRIS Lab and co-developed recovery methods published at top robotics conferences. Toget

orchestra.text:
### Self-optimizing neocloud that cuts LLM costs by 100x
Orchestra is an inference cloud. We capture your AI work traces, train smaller models, and automatically deploy them (only when they outperform the expensive model you are currently paying for). Instead of renting the same frontier model forever, your AI infrastructure gets faster, smarter, and cheaper every time it runs. Suppose your product uses Claude for a repetitive legal workflow. Orchestra observes successful production runs, learns the specific tools and judgment required for that workflow, and trains a specialized open-weight model. Once that model matches or beats Claude on a held-out evaluation, Orchestra starts routing production traffic to it. As more work is completed, the model keeps improving. We started Orchestra because we believe every company using AI should be accumulating intelligence, not accumulating API bills.

**TLDR:** Synapse Semiconductor builds image sensors that process **AI on the sensor** itself. Each pixel captures light and runs neural-network computation in the same device, replacing the need for a GPU while cutting the power and latency of edge vision.
A camera has no use by itself. Its value is only when its information gets evaluated. How can a camera that only has value when combined with a GPU support local intelligence? GPUs will get better, yet the fundamental problem is the separation of the camera and the GPU. Solving that separation will unlock bountiful innovation in machine perception.
**RETINA: a chip designed like the human retina which runs neural network operations in the camera pixel.**
We have compressed the whole edge AI vision hardware stack into **one wafer**. CNNS, VLMS, etc can run on just one chip that senses light. Our compute transistors are also the same photosensors that see light. There is no longer separation between compute (Nvidia Jetson Nano) and a camera (RealSense Depth Camera).

### I picked voice stacks by trial and error for four years
A voice agent is three models in a row: speech-to-text, then an LLM, then text-to-speech. Three vendors, a dozen credible options each. You run a bake-off, you argue about whose numbers are real, and you ship the combination that felt best that month.
Then next week another model drops. And another. Nobody has time to re-run the bake-off, so the stack you picked under deadline quietly becomes the stack you are stuck with for a year.
That is how most voice agents are running today. Not on the best models. On the models that were best whenever someone last had a free week.
Public leaderboards do not settle it either. They are averages over somebody else's audio, in somebody else's conditions. https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AjC8WVA96kUBdD09RJMUgFfvxGfxPvL-/
### We measure, then we route
We benchmark the speech models people actually ship on, language by language, and publish everything at benchmarks.speko.ai: word error rate, finalize latency, time to first token, cost per minute. When a vendor ships a new model we test it the same day and the board updates.

### Vibecode + deploy HIPAA-compliant internal tools, no eng team needed
Floracene lets any healthcare operator describe the internal tool they need and deploy it in one click - connected to production data, with read and write access scoped by the user. Think Lovable or Retool, except purpose-built for the needs of healthcare business that has no engineering team. The bottleneck in healthcare isn't building anymore. Anyone can vibecode an 80% solution in an afternoon, custom to their own workflow, with people already on staff. The tool then dies locally on the builder's computer, because IT (correctly) won't let anyone deploy a tool touching PHI without first-class authentication and permissioning. Our first customer had multiple employees who had each built useful tools and dashboards locally, but couldn't actually share these with coworkers or connect to their core practice data. Within weeks of implementing Floracene, they were able to consolidate their BI tooling into Floracene and shipped 4 net-new to production. A staggering ~$200B is spent on administrative software in healthcare every year in the US. Tens of thousands of those companies still run core operations on spreadsheets, and we're at the top of the first inning of AI adoption. Asaph and Jonah met on the hospitals team at Palantir two years ago, and have each spent the last four years in the plumbing of US healthcare: claims, eligibility, and payor contracting. Asaph was an early PM at Garner. Jonah was a founding engineer at Metriport (YC S22) after starting his own fax-automation startup for fertility clinics.

Hey YC! We're Mark and Trishala, founders of Evident Machines.
We're introducing FrontierEE Bench, the first benchmark to test frontier AI capability on real-world electrical engineering work at a physical lab bench.
**The real world is messy.** Measurements are noisy, components vary, and circuits behave in ways a simulation does not capture. In EE, today's frontier AI models are trained exclusively in simulation and lack the nuance needed to run real-world EE workflows at scale.
**We built our own electronics lab and a custom harness to investigate that gap.** In our lab, models control instruments, direct experiments, and iterate on physical measurements. Human operators carry out requested wiring and probe changes. We record their decisions, measurements, and experimental outcomes.
uploaded image
**FrontierEE Bench** **is a collection of 10 EE tasks that run flawlessly in simulation and fail in the physical world.** Across disciplines like mixed-signal circuits, power systems, and electromechanics the average model pass rate was just 29.3%, with Fable 5.2 reaching a 36.7% pass rate. Models most commonly failed by building open circuits, ignoring stored charge, attempting to bypass current limits, and calculating component properties from incomplete models.
**All of the model failures we discover become RL environments for the frontier labs to train on.** We're building the training infra for autonomous hardware R&D by shaping the models to design, test, and iterate on nuanced EE experiments.

Riften is an independent AI research lab exploring intelligence in software and the physical world. We study how models learn and represent knowledge, and build systems that put that research to work. Our work spans model routing, evaluations, post-training, and physical AI. Earned intelligence.

Riften Launch Video
## What Riften does
Riften is an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible gateway that routes each LLM request to the lowest-cost model capable of completing it.
Connect your existing providers, change the base URL, and keep the product you already built. Riften works across customer-facing AI products and internal tools, including Claude Code and Codex.
**Riften is already removing enterprise-scale model spend from production workloads.**
## Why we built it
Most AI products choose a model once and send nearly everything to it.
A documentation lookup, a support classification, and a codebase migration do not require the same intelligence. Yet they are routinely sent to the same frontier model at the same price.
For customer-facing products, that cost cuts directly into gross margin. For internal agents, it limits how broadly the company can deploy them.
## How it works
Riften evaluates each request locally, applies the company's cost, capability, latency, and reliability constraints, and selects among the models available to that organization.
Hard tasks can still reach frontier models. Routine work moves to lower-cost commercial or open-weight models. Teams can keep their provider accounts, pin a specific model when needed, and inspect the cost and routing decision behind every request.
The objective is not the cheapest token. It is the lowest expected cost of completing the work.
## From routing to company-owned models
The router reveals which work is repeated. Outcomes reveal whether it was done correctly.
A passing test, an accepted patch, a resolved ticket, or a completed workflow can become part of a customer-specific evaluation. Riften uses those evaluations to improve routing, post-train open models around recurring work, and test those models against the APIs they are intended to replace.

Dialogus replaces traditional contact center operations with AI voice agents that can answer calls, resolve customer requests end-to-end, integrate with enterprise systems, and scale across hundreds of locations while maintaining a consistent customer experience.
Today, Dialogus is already powering AI voice operations for Fortune 500 enterprises, handling thousands of customer calls in production.
The company was founded by Rodrigo Teran, Hans Ibarra, and Juberth Rodriguez after seeing how legacy contact center software wasn't built for the AI era. Instead of layering AI on top of decades-old infrastructure, they're building an AI-native contact center from the ground up.

### Network for Physical AI Data Business
Physical AI - robots and world models - is bottlenecked on one thing: diverse, real-world data at massive scale showing how humans actually do work in the physical world. It was never written down, and you can't buy it, because no one has ever captured it. Only real local experts, the people who do this work every day, can produce data this authentic and valuable. DeepReach builds the network that reaches them. We design and manufacture wearable stereo capture devices, then place them with local data partners who run collection as their own business - in warehouses, workshops, farms, kitchens and repair shops. They own the local relationships; we supply the hardware, the software platform, the quality pipeline and the payments. Anyone can run a data business. That structure is what produces diversity. Instead of thousands of hours inside one environment, we deliver hours spread across thousands of environments - which is what actually makes robot policies generalize. 475 devices in the field and 100+ data partners are live across 7 countries, adding new partners every week. They've collected nearly 150,000 clips in the past three months, with volume roughly doubling month over month. Our data is in production with multiple frontier model and robotics companies, and we're scaling to 10,000+ devices across 50 countries.

### Institutional Learning Layer for Every Agent in Your Company
Glen is the layer that unifies every agent your company runs. Glen pulls in agent sessions from Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, plus Slack messages, GitHub prs, tickets, docs and calls. When a new agent picks up a task, Glen finds relevant prior context and injects it in the agents context window to steer it, producing knowledge work that is significantly higher quality, faster and cheaper. Glen does more. You can query the original agent behind any line of code, or search every session your org has ever run. It distills what your team does into skills and surfaces the right one automatically. Agents work multiplayer, picking up the style and context of whoever else is on the file. Transcripts are unified across Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, so you can hand a session from one to another mid-task. And Glen can also double as a company brain, from Slack, in app, or by just installing Glen on any agent. We're building toward a future where memory is no longer the missing piece of intelligence. A future where every agent maintains a lossless and continuous thread of institutional experience enabling the era of the compounding organization and fully unsupervised digital labour.

See original launch post
Hi everyone,
I'm Michael, founder of Codag.
**TL;DR:** Codag compresses tool results before models read them, lowering costs and improving accuracy without changing how developers work, while providing tool usage analytics.
https://youtu.be/eJbK3SezeXA
### The problem
Agents consume huge amounts of output from searches, tests, builds, logs, file trees, and APIs.
A single tool result can add thousands of mostly repetitive lines to a session. The model processes that output before provider-native compaction can help. Important evidence gets buried, so the agent searches again, retries, or rereads the same data.
This makes agent sessions slower and more expensive. Companies also lack a consistent view of which tools and MCP servers agents use across Claude Code, Codex, and other harnesses.
### What Codag does
Codag attaches to existing agent harnesses with one setup command.
It handles each result according to the action being performed:
- Tests preserve failures, traces, file locations, and exit status.
- Searches preserve exact file and line references.
- Logs preserve chronology, causal evidence, and outliers.
- Anything omitted remains selectively retrievable.
Optimized tool results are 75% smaller on average, while preserving signal.
Developers keep working normally. Codag reduces what reaches the model before the model pays to read it.
Codag also reports which tools and MCP servers agents invoke, along with tokens, model-adjusted spend, savings, reducer cost, and latency across providers. Because Codag already sits in the tool path, it becomes the natural place for companies to control which tools agents can use, under what policies, and at what cost.
### Results so far
More than 90 organizations use Codag, including teams of up to 35 people. I built and sold the product solo.

Token spend is growing and it's growing fast. Out of 100+ companies we spoke to, most are trying to cut their inference costs.
Reserved capacity guarantee deals provide discounts + certainty, but are negotiated bilaterally, take time, and are **hard to switch from** - as a buyer you commit by prepayment, which you lose if you switch to a different provider, or in some cases even a different model.
What if a buyer could:
1. See all possible discounted capacity deals in one place

2. Selling future capacity is an excellent way to finance GPU compute - dilution-free and interest-free
3. Extra distribution channel for enterprise buyers

screenpipe records what you do, see and hear on your computer, makes it searchable, and gives agents the context to understand how you actually work. The project has 20K+ GitHub stars.
https://youtu.be/c1jV6E9pyug
Most AI agents start every task with partial context.
They can read the prompt and apps you connect. They do not remember the meeting where a decision was made, the tab you opened last Tuesday, the exact steps you took to fix a problem, or the edge case you discovered while doing the work.
screenpipe runs quietly in the background and captures screen and audio context on your machine. Then you can ask:
- maintain a second brain for every person, projects, tasks, meetings
- turn the workday into a daily recap and time breakdown for standups or client billing
- maintain a personal CRM from the people, conversations, and follow-ups seen during the day
- find commitments mentioned in meetings or messages that never made it into a task list
- analyze repeated work and produce a list of workflows worth automating
- save prompts and context from Claude, Codex, and ChatGPT into a searchable journal
Agents can use screenpipe as long-term memory, so they work from what actually happened instead of only what you remembered to paste into a prompt.
The same foundation also works across team machines. Teams can map repeated workflows, generate SOPs, find bottlenecks, and identify automation opportunities across the tools where work actually happens.
screenpipe is open source and local-first. You control what gets recorded, can exclude apps, windows, and URLs, and choose where your data lives.
I've been building my own AI second brain since 2020, but it could only remember what I explicitly saved. I built screenpipe so my AI could understand what I was actually doing across my screen and conversations. Other people began using it for the same reason. Today, we're turning that foundation into context for personal and team agents.

### Making chemicals 100,000x faster
We build foundational AI models for chemistry. Almost nothing you buy is a single chemical. Products like datacenter coolant, GPU thermal paste, paint, and glue are formulations, which are mixtures of around ten ingredients each, and demand for them has grown quickly because of AI and EVs. Designing a new formulation is essentially a search problem, because there are more possible mixtures than anyone could ever test, and none of them can be predicted in advance. As a result, bringing a single formulation to market today takes three to five years of trial and error in a lab. Our models predict how a mixture will behave far faster than the standard methods used today, which lets us design new formulations in weeks rather than years, at a fraction of the cost. To prove this, we used them to invent three chemicals that never existed before, including a PFAS-free coolant for datacenters, and we have since synthesized and patented all three. We are already working with some of the largest manufacturers to design formulations for them, and we are building our own lab to generate the data that will train our next models.

definite.text:
### Connect operational data with finance to see what drives the numbers.
Definite connects operational data with finance so businesses that make, move, build or operate things can see what each production run, load and job actually cost. These businesses already record a lot: production runs, shipments, job sites, equipment hours, work orders. Finance records the same business in a different shape. Operating systems track activity by site, line, or day. The ledger tracks it by entity, account, and month. Both sets of records exist, but the link between an operating decision and its financial effect usually lives in spreadsheets and in a few people's heads. So questions that should be routine take days. What happens to cash if one plant adds a shift? How does a change in throughput or staffing flow into the forecast? Which operating changes actually moved the numbers last quarter? Definite connects to existing operational and financial systems read-only. Models propose how operational records map to financial ones and explain what they find. Deterministic rules perform the calculations and checks, so results trace back to the source records they came from. Definite started in a plant office an hour from campus, watching a controller rebuild the same spreadsheet she rebuilds every month to tie her production system to her ledger. The three of us met at the University of Waterloo and had each spent our careers on a version of that join. Gurshabd built wallet policy and approval controls at BitGo, where proving customer assets matched the ledger was still done by hand. Farhan built recommendation systems for Instagram Reels at Meta, joining billions of raw events to the numbers the business reported. Mazin built trading systems at Optiver, then agents for financial analysts at Boosted.ai, where analysts would not act on a number they could not trace. In finance that work is at least funded. In companies that make and move things, nobody had built it at all.

EdotEnv (YC S26) turn markets into self-improving research environments for AI agents.
The path to RSI is a continuous loop: agents conduct experiments, learn from the results, and autonomously become better at conducting the next round of research. For that loop to continue, each round must present a harder problem than the last.
Markets create this dynamic naturally. Every discovered inefficiency attracts competition, and every successful strategy makes future opportunities harder to find. Markets therefore provide an advancing frontier for self-improving agents.
EdotEnv captures this process in multi-step environments where agents form hypotheses, design experiments, verify results and iterate. They use these environments to evaluate and post-train agents on increasingly difficult research tasks.
They work with frontier AI labs and academic groups building research harnesses, evaluation benchmarks, and post-training environments.
EdotEnv's team previously worked in quantitative research at G-Research, high frequency options trading at TransMarket Group, and LLM inference research at Etched.
If you're working on RSI, RL, post-training, or AI for research, reach out to them at info@edotenv.com.

**The Idea**
Advancement in AI relies on chips. Transformers won because they mapped well to GPUs. Frontier Labs are now co-designing their own silicon to maximize intelligence/joule.
It takes years and 100s of experts to bring a chip from architecture through tape-out.
Our goal as a company is to push the frontier of AI on chip design tasks - enabling advanced chips to be taped-out by small teams in months.
We also believe this is the path forward to achieving true recursive self-improvement (RSI). Where AI designs better chips and better chips train more intelligent AI.
To achieve this, we're building **RL Environments For Long-Horizon Chip Design.**
Our environments enable 1000s of parallel rollouts for training on chip design tasks. We also curate a private held-out test set for performing evals in the environment to compare model capabilities.
uploaded image
**What Exists**
Chip design should be a perfect domain for this type of RL. Instead:
- The academic benchmarks are one-shot puzzles of ~100 lines, and they're in every training set.
- The field's de facto standard (NVIDIA's CVDP) has saturated - going from 34% to 97% once agents could iterate against the grader.
- The published tasks are short-horizon and graded by running testbenches. In one study, designs that passed their bundled testbenches 95-97% of the time were only ~20% correct under formal checking.
And none of it resembles the real loop: months of work, tools in the loop, and hard trade-offs between latency, throughput, area, and power.
**What We Build**
Our RL Environment is designed for long-horizon chip design tasks.
- **Long-horizon.** One episode is the real loop: choose a microarchitecture, write the RTL, simulate, synthesize, check timing and power, revise.

TLDR: machine0 is a CLI for agent compute: "machine0 new mybox" gives your agent a full cloud VM, billed by the minute, from $0.013/hr up to 60 vCPU / 240 GB and 8×H100s. Agents drive it themselves via CLI or MCP.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gyllkZ0M04E
## The Pain
Agent workloads are moving from ephemeral to always-on. A coding agent working on a hard feature runs 6-8 hours. Auto-research agents run for days. OpenClaw & Hermes run 24/7. As you run more in parallel:
- **Resources**: a few agents on a big codebase saturate your RAM and CPU. Auto-research needs GPUs you don't have.
- **Security**: "-yolo" on your personal machine is one prompt injection away from exfiltrated credentials.
- **Availability**: close your laptop and the agent dies mid-task.
- **Isolation**: there's no clean line between everything on your laptop and the minimum this agent actually needs.
## The Solution
machine0 gives every agent its own computer. It's a CLI that both humans and agents can use without reading docs:
- "machine0 new mybox" creates an SSH-ready VM with a static IP and HTTPS endpoint. Always on (99.99% uptime) until you switch it off.
- **Billed by the minute.** 1 vCPU / 1 GB at $0.013/hr up to 60 vCPU / 240 GB, plus GPUs from RTX 4000 Ada to 8×H100s.
- **Profiles.** Bundles of MCP connections, credentials, prompts, and env vars, injected at VM creation. Each agent gets exactly the capabilities (or personality) you choose, and nothing else.
- **Agents self-serve.** Hand the CLI or MCP server to Claude, Codex, or OpenCode and it manages its own fleet: spin up a box for a build, snapshot it, tear it down.
- **Suspend & resume.** Pause an idle machine, stop paying for compute, resume exactly where it left off.
- **Snapshot & clone.** Configure one machine perfectly, then stamp out ten identical agents from it.

AI agents still fail on real work: the messy, multi-tool, permission-heavy workflows inside actual companies. aerogen-systems.title: Public page
aerogen-systems.text:
### Modernizing Chip Manufacturing Infrastructure
We are building the future of chip manufacturing. Chips are more advanced than ever, and the features inside them keep getting smaller. But the cleanroom infrastructure supporting their manufacture has not scaled at the same pace. Intel, TSMC, Samsung, and others spend billions building and operating massive cleanrooms, only to isolate their most advanced wafers from the surrounding facility as much as possible. We think that architecture is backwards. Instead of making the entire building cleaner, why not make the machinery itself as clean as possible? Talos is our proprietary tool-integrated purification system. It sits directly inside semiconductor equipment and continuously destroys airborne molecular contaminants before they reach the wafer. Instead of fighting contamination by constantly flooding tools with ultra-high-purity nitrogen, Talos keeps the environment inside the machine 10-100x cleaner, without the massive purge-gas bill. Talos is powerful on its own, but it is also the foundation for a much bigger vision: the Cleanpipe. The Aerogen Systems Cleanpipe is an ultra-clean interconnect infrastructure that protects wafers as they move from machine to machine across the fab. Rather than relying on a billion-dollar cleanroom to protect every cubic foot of factory space, Cleanpipe creates a controlled environment only where cleanliness actually matters: around the wafer. Talos cleans the tools. Cleanpipe connects them. Eventually, we delete the cleanroom and build more advanced chips, at greater scale, with radically less infrastructure. With cleanpipes connecting tools, chip fabs can exist anywhere.

##### We're building the most token-efficient coding agent in the world. The reason it works is GitNexus, our open-source knowledge graph for your codebase.
https://youtu.be/-ErU4cCRSlQ
##### The problem
Coding agents don't understand your repo. They grep, they guess, they re-read the same files, and they stuff half your codebase into a context window hoping the answer is in there somewhere. You pay for every one of those tokens, and the agent still misses the cross-file relationship that mattered.
The bottleneck isn't the model. It's context.
##### What we built:
GitNexus indexes your repository into a knowledge graph (symbols, call paths, imports, ownership, history) and serves the agent exactly the context a task needs, instead of everything it might need.
It's one connected stack:
- The knowledge graph. Run npx gitnexus analyze and you have it
- A coding agent that runs on top of it
- Automated PR review grounded in the same graph
uploaded image
##### The proof:
On the DeepSWE benchmark, we ran the same agent with our graph and without it:
- 37% to 68.4% pass rate. Nearly twice the bugs solved
- Half the cost per fix, with fewer tokens
- On the hardest tasks, the gap more than triples
Full methodology and results: https://www.akonlabs.com/benchmarks
##### Where we are:
- 45,000+ GitHub stars
- 65,000 weekly npm downloads
- 10+ enterprises onboarded
##### About the team:
Subham Kundu and Abhigyan Patwari have spent nearly half a decade working on knowledge graphs. Between them, they've been founding engineers, CTOs, and principal AI engineers, taking products from 0 to 100 at multiple startups. Subham is a seasoned engineer who has scaled products to millions of users, won multiple hackathons, and doing a PhD in reinforcement learning. fabraix.text:
### The world's frontier hacker of AI agents.
Fabraix builds state-of-the-art AI red-teaming agents that continuously detect security vulnerabilities in customer-facing AI. Our product, Nyx, has already found vulnerabilities in agents at dozens of Fortune 500 companies. AI agents can change more often than teams can test them. A new model, prompt, tool, permission, or data source can change what an agent does, even when the application code stays the same. And AI is also increasing how much software companies produce and how often it changes. We built Nyx to automate the work required to red-team AI agents. It is multi modal by design and interacts with the target indirectly through controlled replicas of SaaS products and websites that we maintain, placing malicious payloads in webpages, documents, files, messages, and tool outputs to test how an agent behaves under different conditions. We're also the team behind ACE (Adversarial Cost to Exploit), a benchmark that measures AI security in terms of how much it costs attackers to break an AI system; providing a game-theoretic framework to understand how motivated a rational attacker would be in exploiting the system.

**TLDR:** Risklytics is a commercial insurance brokerage for companies building with AI in the physical space, from robot fleets on customer sites to agents running in production. This year many insurance companies stopped covering risks that involve AI. We find the insurers that will still cover it, translate what you're building into terms they can price, and read every clause before anything is signed.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jHTzpKbmZa4
**The problem**
Starting this year, many insurance companies began excluding coverage for injury and property damage arising out of AI.
For a hardtech company that language reaches everything you do. If AI touched the work anywhere, including the tools your engineers designed it with or the product itself, the insurer can deny the claim.
The problem with these exclusions is that they get added account by account, so the same hardware can be covered at one insurer and excluded at the next, and nothing in the process makes that obvious. It shows up as a form number on the endorsement list attached to your renewal, which is why most founders don't learn they have one until they file a claim.
**Why now**
Physical AI is scaling faster than the insurance market underneath it. Insurance moves slower, and its first instinct with an unfamiliar risk is to exclude it and wait for loss data. Cyber went the same way: exclusions first, then specialists who understood it, then a real market. AI is at the exclusion stage now, and these companies pushing the frontier can't wait for the cycle to finish on its own.

The technologies that define this century, including data centers, rockets, satellites, and robots, are built from complex metal parts. As these systems advance, the parts get harder to make. Past a certain complexity, casting and machining stop working, and the advanced methods that remain are slow, expensive, and hazardous. Ultrasonium has invented a new manufacturing method to make these critical parts 15x faster and 75% cheaper than the methods they replace, in the U.S. and at scale. Solid metal feedstock goes in and a finished part safely comes out, controlled by a physical AI layer and novel control processes. The systems that matter most, in aerospace, energy, and compute, are demanding metal geometries that can't be machined or cast and are too expensive and slow to make with incumbent methods, at a moment when domestic manufacturing capacity is a national priority. Executor.sh is an MCP gateway that allows you to sign in once to all of your integrations and use them with any client. We enable you to connect your agents to anything (MCP, GraphQL, OpenAPI) so regardless of what you're trying to connect agents to you're able to. https://youtu.be/NWYFpDW02Dw
## The problem
You don't have one agent anymore. You have Claude Code, a ChatGPT account, Cursor, maybe a box in the corner running jobs overnight. Three problems follow:
1. **Every agent wants its own OAuth into everything.** You connect your calendar to the tenth harness in a slightly different way, tokens expire, connectors deprecate, and each agent is missing something when you need it.
2. **Most connectors stop at one account per service.** One Google login means your agent sees your work calendar or your personal one, never both. Your flights land in one inbox, your meetings in the other, and no agent can reason over your actual day.
3. **Permissions are an afterthought.** Once an agent holds a token, it can do anything that token allows. Giving an agent your email shouldn't mean trusting it to never hit delete.
## What Executor does
Connect once in Executor, and sever all the one-off connections.
Each integration gets credentials plus a per-tool policy: **always allowed**, **needs approval**, or **blocked**. Point any MCP-compatible agent at Executor and it has everything.
- **All your accounts, not just one.** Accounts are connections: work and personal Gmail, two calendars, a staging and a production Stripe, side by side. Every agent sees all of them.
- **One tool shape.** MCP, OpenAPI, and GraphQL integrations all normalize into a consistent name + schema. 1,600+ tools collapse into a single ~1k-token surface instead of ~280k tokens of tool definitions.

RonanRX is a full-stack pharmaceutical company, starting with personalized peptides and GLP-1s. In our first 10 weeks, we went from having no pharmacy to being licensed in 33 states. Before AI, doing this for every patient at scale was impossible. We didn't invent the demand we are seeing. 80 Million people are on a GLP-1 and millions more are using Peptides. We're building a better way to manufacture, personalize, prescribe, and deliver them. Our founders have built and exited multiple companies, raised more than $100M, built a $50M U.S. medical manufacturing business, and spent years developing peptide therapeutics at companies including Eli Lilly and AbbVie. - Delivered over REST, an MCP server, and webhooks. Works out of the box with Claude, ChatGPT, Hermes, and OpenClaw.
You can ship our data inside your own product. Redistribution included, no per-seat pricing, no anti-AI usage restrictions.

Hi, we're Computable, the first exchange for physical compute where you can buy, sell, and use GPU capacity for exactly the dates you want like staying on Airbnb. You pay less, commit less, and stay flexible.

Compute is the newest major commodity, but it still trades like an asset from the last century. You overpay going in and you eat the weeks you don't use.

We put a public price on every week. Open the market and you'll see dedicated H100 nodes, every week through January 2027, each with its own price, from $2.55/GPU-hr. Pick a start week and an end week, and it's yours.

- **Sell back what you don't use.** If your plans change, sell the weeks back to the market whenever you want; we keep a market quote posted on every position.
- **Lock next year at a price you can see.** January 2027 is on the grid today, so you know exactly what the future run costs before another H100 40% rate jump happens.
- **Real machines, fast.** Dedicated H100 SXM nodes, full SSH root access, live within an hour of your window start.
**Why us**
Our founding team comes from Jump Trading, Coinbase, Citadel Securities, and other trading firms and exchanges. We have spent our careers building markets. Stay tuned for more products coming soon as we build out the financial infrastructure of the AI economy.

### Curing cancer. Starting with dogs.
Gamgee began with Rosie, founder Paul Conyngham's dog. After surgery, chemotherapy and immunotherapy failed, Rosie was given months to live. Paul used AI and genomic analysis to identify targets in her tumour, then worked with scientists at UNSW to produce what is believed to be the first fully computationally designed mRNA cancer vaccine delivered to a dog. Following treatment, several tumours shrank significantly and her quality of life improved Gamgee is building an end to end platform for personalised mRNA cancer vaccines for dogs. We sequence a dog's tumour and healthy DNA, identify mutations unique to its cancer, and design a vaccine that teaches the immune system what to attack. We manage the entire process- from vet intake and tissue collection through genomic analysis, vaccine production, treatment and response monitoring We are now turning that one off effort into a repeatable clinical system. Gamgee is running clinical trials in Australia, working with vets, oncologists and specialised laboratories, and accepting cases globally. ### Training company-specific models that approve AI actions.
An agent's access should depend on the task it is doing. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another. Access decisions need to adapt in real time as the agent works, but companies can't turn every business judgment into a fixed rules or have people manually approve every step. We train small, company-specific models that approve AI actions in real time. They consider the company's policies and interests, the agent's current task, and its past actions to decide whether each proposed action should be allowed. Access is specific to the task at hand and reassessed as the agent works. Companies will rent intelligence from AI labs or run open-source models to power their agents. They'll own the models that keep their entire AI workforce acting in their interests. Decawork is building those models.

**Hi Everyone!**
**We're Niki and Thomas - cofounders of Lamb Labs.**
**TL;DR: We build custom AI inference chips that run inference at 20,000+ tok/s and 63x higher intelligence per watt than a traditional GPU. Fully local and private by construction, no subscriptions, no API costs.**
**Our mission: the world's fastest LLM at the lowest power.**
https://youtu.be/MhhY1Dy9ltE?feature=shared
**Our hot take: AI models are finally getting good enough to hardcode them directly into silicon.** Once you stop treating the chip as a general-purpose GPU and burn a specific model into hardware, inference gets radically faster and cheaper per watt. Most of the industry is still building flexible, general chips. We think that flexibility is exactly what's wasting your energy. So we're on a mission to reduce the energy footprint of AI.
**The Problem**
AI is taking power on two fronts: concentrating control of data and intelligence, and consuming ever more electricity to grow. That future scares us, so we're building against it.
Here's the technical root of the waste: **GPUs burn most of their energy during inference moving data, not computing.** LLM/VLM inference is memory-bound, fetching a weight from memory costs ~100-1000x the energy of the arithmetic you do with it. So you underutilize the GPU you paid for: some GPUs only hit 20-40% compute utilization during LLM inference while the rest idles waiting on memory.

**TL;DR:** For companies running large fleets of OS-level endpoints (running GPU clusters, having a network of cloud devices, or deploying on-device), Palisade detects and fixes operating-system vulnerabilities (privilege escalation, remote code execution, memory corruption) that are extremely hard to detect and mitigate without applying AI to kernel-level data (syscalls, eBPF traces, process/memory events, network packets). A fix that used to take weeks to roll out, Palisade now applies in minutes across every endpoint.
Hey YC! I'm Prince, an ML researcher and engineer who dropped out from Caltech at 18 to build Palisade.
**What's the problem:** Modern attacks increasingly target the operating system, but most security products only observe the network, cloud, or application layers. That leaves OS vulnerabilities among the hardest problems to detect and the slowest to remediate across a fleet.
**Why I'm building this:** Since I was 16, I have done plenty of professional red-team and blue-team security work. One pattern kept showing up: OS-level vulnerabilities were consistently the hardest to handle. Detection required low-level visibility, and even after identifying a vulnerability, rolling out a mitigation across hundreds or thousands of machines often took weeks. My background in both machine learning and operating systems convinced me this didn't have to be a manual process, so I built Palisade to automatically detect and remediate these vulnerabilities at the kernel level across an entire fleet.
**What Palisade does:** Palisade watches your systems at the kernel level-syscalls, eBPF traces, process and memory events, and network packets-and uses AI to find OS vulnerabilities other tools miss, then implement the fix automatically across every endpoint.

### AI engineer that debugs and fixes production incidents in realtime
With tools like Cursor and Claude Code, writing software is no longer the bottleneck. Debugging is. Agents cannot fix production crashes using logs and traces that were sized for human eyeballs. The gap is missing data. HyperProbe allows agents to debug live software autonomously. Our SDK drops non-breaking probes straight into running services to read exact variable states from memory at the moment of failure, instead of reasoning backwards from flat logs. Zero redeploys. Under 1% CPU overhead. Automatic PII redaction. We turn 4-hour production war rooms into 10-minute automated resolutions. As agents write and operate more of the world's software, HyperProbe is the runtime observability layer that lets them understand what they built.

I'm Damian, founder of Skymerse (S26). I'm a licensed flight dispatcher and have spent 10 years working across flight operations, aviation data, and software.
We're building one AI system to automate flight operations - from planning and monitoring in the operations center to real-time support in the cockpit.
Our goal is full automation of the work behind every flight.
https://youtu.be/czP5N1FJ1ds
## The problem
Airlines have spent decades digitizing flight operations. The information moved from paper to screens. The work of understanding it did not. A flight exists across many systems. Each system may be good at its own job, but the complete operational picture exists between them.
Pilots and operations teams still have to build that picture themselves. They search, compare, and interpret information to plan, monitor, and adapt every flight from schedule to landing.
When something changes, they do it again. When responsibility moves from the operations center to the crew, much of the context has to be passed on or rebuilt.
Today, people are the integration layer.
## What Skymerse does
Skymerse builds a live operational model of every flight. When an airline's schedule flows in, it assembles the operational context for each flight and keeps it current as conditions change.
That model is the foundation for automation. Skymerse does not stop at displaying information or sending an alert. It understands what a change means for the flight, updates the operation, and carries the required work forward automatically.
Skymerse plans, monitors, and adapts flights from the operations center to the cockpit. Instead of rebuilding context across tools and handoffs, Skymerse manages each flight as one continuous process, from schedule to landing.

Today we're introducing Locke, an applied AI company changing the way companies and governments work together. Our first focus: building an AI-native government affairs firm that helps companies monitor regulations, lobby policymakers, and win government contracts.
American governments spend over $10 trillion a year - and it's all up for grabs, reallocated annually through budgets, appropriations, and contracts. Its front door is guarded by legacy government affairs firms that charge incumbent prices, and their customers get a fragmented product: one firm for the Hill, another for agencies, another for proposals and procurement, with no one accountable for the outcome.
Locke is building the front door government never had. We combine our AI agents with in-house lobbyists who own the entire path - from research to first meeting to funded contract. On the backend, our agents make the path faster than ever - analyzing legislation, tracking stakeholder engagement, and drafting complex contract proposals.
Since quietly launching six weeks ago, we've blown past a $500K annual revenue run-rate serving clients across defense, healthcare, GovTech, and more.
Locke was founded by Parth Badhwar, who came to this problem from both sides of the table: policy roles at the White House and Deloitte, then leading GTM at a startup that sold to dozens of government offices. The team is small, talent-dense, and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch.
Locke's mission is bigger than replacing lobbying firms. It's a future where winning government support depends on what you make, not who you know.
It's day one in that mission.

### Telemetry storage for the agentic era.
Limnion is building an open-standards telemetry storage platform for observability at scale, including agentic workflows. Siglake is the open-source project that sits at the heart of it, designed around OTel, Parquet, and Iceberg. No proprietary storage, no vendor lock-in.
Company Launches
Limnion: Telemetry storage built for the agentic era
See original launch post
**Modern observability is dying.**
https://youtu.be/eE0DmtIGSsw
Limnion is building telemetry storage for the agentic era. Our open-source foundation, Siglake, stores your logs and traces in open formats in your own cloud storage, so your AI agents can query them directly with SQL. No vendor lock-in, no proprietary API in the way. Here's why I think this is what observability needs.
Gone are the days of humans building dashboards by hand, scrubbing through log lines, and manually tuning alert thresholds. Agents are becoming the primary consumers of telemetry - and when you actually need to look at a dashboard, an agent can create one on the fly. My prediction: 90% of human-centric observability work disappears within two years.
Observability isn't becoming less valuable - it's more valuable than ever. What's changing is who it's for. The tooling we have today was built for one job: making vast amounts of data understandable to humans. Once humans are no longer the primary consumers, the entire paradigm changes.
Traditional observability won't disappear, but will instead shrink into something much narrower: a thin governance layer. Humans will still watch the handful of genuinely critical systems and keep an eye on the agentic layer itself to make sure it's doing its job. Someone has to watch the watchers. Everything else migrates to agent-native platforms.
The stakes are big. Gartner expects observability platforms to be a ~$14B market by 2028 - Datadog alone is guiding to ~$4.5B in revenue this year - and 44% of Gartner clients already spend more than $1M a year on observability. My bet is that most of that value migrates to the agentic layer, leaving legacy observability as a governance market that's a fraction of its current size.
That migration is the opportunity - and today's vendors are on the wrong side of it. Observability vendors, by and large, extract enormous sums for walled gardens that were never built for agentic consumption. They are not - and never will be - incentivized to give your agents wide-open access to the underlying data. Their business model depends on keeping it locked in.
The agentic era needs the opposite: telemetry storage that's open by design and built for agents first. That's Siglake.

Agents never hold real secrets: the credential is injected at the network layer, per request, after the call is authorized. You can't steal what isn't there.

Lately, autonomous agents have arrived and shown up everywhere. Tools like OpenClaw and Hermes have become extremely popular and been adopted by open source communities, mostly by individuals. Companies, however, have been left behind: they need integration with their identity providers to enable easy provisioning of agents on behalf of an employee's identity, with least-privilege access.
Those tools have fundamental flaws. Security fundamentals, like secret handling and organization-level control, are missing by default. So companies must choose between weak agents or making them powerful but risky.
✅ **What OneCLI Does**
OneCLI gives teams the whole harness, open source and self-hosted, so agents can be powerful and safe at once:
- **Sandboxed agent per employee:** each agent runs isolated with its own memory, skills, and permissions.
- **Secrets injected at the network layer:** the agent gets a placeholder, the gateway swaps in the real credential per request, after the call is authorized. Credentials never enter the agent's context, memory, or logs.

# **TL;DR:**
**VIM is Sentry for industrial automation cells. When a cell faults, VIM reads the error code and the live machine signals, digs the root cause out of the OEM manuals and the cell's own history, and stages one safe fix for the operator to approve. When a CNC drifts, VIM catches it with the machine's own probe seconds after the cut and stages the offset correction. Downtime goes from hours to about a minute; scrap gets caught at part one instead of final inspection.**
Watch how **VIM** works:
Robot Cell Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JfGQjorNS2U
CNC Machine Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fgNPOtBLku8
# WHAT WE BUILT
VIM sits on the cell and closes the loop from fault to recovery:
1. **Connect**. Reads **PLC**, **HMI**, **robot**, **CNC**, **sensor**, and **driver state** without touching the controls you already trust.
2. **Understand**. Matches the fault to live signals, the right page of the right manual, and this cell's own prior recoveries or trends the probe touches and traces drift to tool wear, thermal growth, a bumped fixture.
3. **Recover**. Stages one bounded, validated action: a restart, a parameter change, an offset correction. The operator approves it like a pull request.

### Evals for robots
Robocurve builds open-source tools and independent benchmarks to measure how well robots can do real-world jobs. Instead of relying on unverified demo videos from frontier labs, we score their models on reproducible benchmarks that anyone can trust. Today there are no well-run, standardized robotics benchmarks. Labs evaluate in-house, and no independent group has stepped in to run continuous benchmarking as a service. The result is that no one actually knows how good anyone else is, or where the real frontier sits. Good benchmarks require operating and maintaining physical hardware and real-world setups. Simulation only goes so far, since models that look strong in sim can show large performance gaps once deployed in the real world. Building real-world benchmarks means coordinating job-domain experts, evals engineering, and hands-on robotics all at once. Frontier labs are targeting general-purpose robotics by 2028, yet the field of robotics evals barely exists. Whoever builds the trusted measure of robot capability becomes the reference everyone relies on. We combine backgrounds in AI evals and robotics to build and grow this field as fast as possible. We already shipped v1 of our open-source framework, Inspect Robots, and ran our first pilot scoring a frontier model on a real robot.

caution.title: Public page
caution.text:
### Hosting platform for software you can't afford to have hacked
Caution is a hosting platform for software you can't afford to get hacked. It simplifies and extends confidential compute, and lets developers deploy workloads to secure enclaves in minutes and give customers, auditors, and counterparties cryptographic proof that production is running the exact reviewed source code, build, configuration, and runtime - not an opaque binary controlled by a cloud operator or internal admin. Confidential computing hardware exists, but the tooling is too fragmented and incomplete for most teams to use well. Today, attestation often proves only that a binary has a certain hash; it does not prove what source code produced that binary. Building the missing deployment, reproducibility, and verification layer requires specialized security engineering and often locks teams into one cloud or hardware stack. Caution turns that into a simple git-based workflow that builds reproducible enclave images, provisions infrastructure, and lets anyone independently verify what is running. We built Caution after years securing high-risk systems through Distrust, where we worked with hedge funds, custodians, blockchain teams, cloud platforms, and critical grid operators on systems responsible for more than $600B in assets. Again and again, the same problem showed up: teams running mission-critical infrastructure could not reliably prove what was executing in production. As AI, fintech, healthcare, and regulated data collaboration move into the cloud, "trust us" is no longer enough. Caution is a general-purpose platform: if it runs on a server, it can run verifiably on Caution. We're starting where trust failures cost the most, but we believe verifiable compute will become the default way software runs, the same way HTTPS became the default way it's served. Infrastructure you can verify, not trust.

Deep in confidential computing, supply chain security, and applied cryptography. Mission: improve the freedom, security, and privacy of as many people as possible.

## **TLDR**
Neomatter is the operating system for in-house legal teams. It plugs into the places your company already works (email, Slack, Salesforce, etc) and picks up legal requests as they come in. When someone sends legal a contract or a question, the work is already done before a lawyer opens it, ready to review and approve. https://youtu.be/delvI16C41E
## **The problem**
Every part of your company runs through legal.
Sales needs contracts signed. HR needs employment agreements. Finance needs board approvals. And every department has legal questions.
But legal teams spend a lot of their time on repetitive work: reviewing the same terms, searching for old agreements, answering familiar questions, and chasing information.
The software tools haven't solved this. One tool manages contracts, another handles requests, and another tracks approvals. Lawyers still have to piece the work together themselves.
And when teams reach capacity, companies hire more lawyers or send work to expensive outside firms.
## **What we're building**
Neomatter takes a request from start to finish. It gathers context, reviews documents, checks the company's policies and precedents, and prepares the work for approval.
## **How it works**
Neomatter monitors the places legal requests already come through (email, Slack, teams, Salesforce, and more) and automatically triages requests to the right lawyer. Nobody has to tag anything or learn a new tool.
Then it does the work. It reads everything, does the redlines, checks it against your team's playbooks, drafts the reply, and waits for your decision. By the time you know the matter exists, 90% of the work has already been done. The lawyer opens finished work, checks the sources, writes any edits, and makes the decision.

Hi everyone, we're Aneesh and Josh.
**TL;DR:** Hue creates stateful clones of the apps your agent connects to, so you can test changes against realistic tools, data, and state before they reach users.
**The problem**
Agents take on real work now: they send emails on our behalf, update CRMs, and issue refunds. But there's usually no safe place to test them. You can't experiment on a user's live inbox, mock APIs aren't representative, and sandbox tenants start empty, so your agent never meets the messy data and business nuance it will see in production. When an agent fails in production, it's difficult to reproduce the issue and verify a fix.
**How Hue solves this**
Hue simulates all the apps your agent might use, like Gmail, Slack, Salesforce, Notion, and Quickbooks. The apps are populated in two ways
- Generate worlds: let your coding agent describe the environment to test against, like the apps of a 40-person software company that just raised their Series B, and Hue populates the apps with months of realistic history within a couple minutes.
- Start from real runs: Hue uses your agent traces to recreate the state of the world during a real run, so you can reproduce agent failures and verify the fix.
Your agent uses these apps just like it uses the real ones, without touching any live accounts. You can run your agent from the same starting point as many times as you need, test it against various situations in minutes, set up evals to measure performance quantitatively, and compare versions before you ship.

herdr.title: Public page
herdr.text:
### building the open agent runtime
Developers don't run one coding agent anymore. They run fleets of them - for hours, sometimes days - across laptops, servers, and sandboxes. Keeping track of that work is the new bottleneck: which agent is blocked, which one finished, which terminal is it in, and why did everything die when the laptop closed. Herdr is the open-source home for that work. A background server owns the agents' terminal sessions on each machine, so the work survives disconnects, closed lids, and dropped SSH. Herdr detects each agent and turns the chaos into an attention queue - working, blocked, done, across every project - so you look only when an agent needs you. Every client is just a view: the bundled terminal UI, SSH from another machine, your phone. Close one, open another; the work never stops. Software can drive it too: a CLI, a socket API, and a plugin marketplace that passed 500 community plugins in its first month. The runtime is Apache-2.0 and stays open. Four months after launch: 25k GitHub stars, 340k downloads.

Petrichor is a wet lab for frontier AI labs. They send us experiments, we run them in parallel and return the data from every step.
Hi everyone, I'm Wille, CEO of Petrichor (F26), building this with my cofounders Elias and Jesper.
**Why** Code and math improved fast because a model can check its own answer. In biology the answer comes out of an experiment, so how many experiments get run sets the limit on how good models can get. We think biology is the most important field AI will touch and at the same time the most data constrained one.
**What we're building** Frontier labs are all going after biology and need far more experiments than they can run themselves, so we run them. Models use the lab directly through our Python library, writing each experiment as a job and submitting it themselves. We capture as much data as we can from every run, so labs end up with the best possible training data for improving their models. Customers own all the data we produce for them, and we never share it or train on it. Every experiment is run by people on our team for safety reasons, and we'll only hand execution over to robots once we're sure that's safe.

### A factory for small and specialized video reasoning models
The world generates petabytes of video every day, and almost none of it is readable to machines. Frontier VLMs that can unlock this (like Gemini) are too expensive to run at the volume real industries have, too generic for any single task, and can't be deployed on-prem where sensitive video lives. We are building an auto vision factory: take video plus a customer's objective, distill a frontier model, and post-train a small open model that is SOTA on that one task and serve it blazingly fast. Our first product, Marlin, is a 2B-parameter open-weights video VLM that matches Gemini-2.5-flash on dense captioning and temporal grounding at a fraction of the cost.

saccade.title: Public page
saccade.text:
### World's Earliest Test for Alzheimer's Biomarkers
Alzheimer's testing today is bottlenecked around the onset of symptoms, when the damage is already done. Current treatments, including the FDA-approved drugs released in 2024, don't reverse the disease; they only slow it down. Earlier detection means earlier intervention. Eye movement changes linked to Alzheimer's surface sooner than any other biomarker, up to 15 years before symptoms appear. We deliver a 15-minute VR assessment delivered to patients in longevity clinics: • Tasks: patients perform visual tasks designed by neurologists to trigger a distinct oculomotor response in people with Alzheimer's or on its path • Hardware: our patent-pending attachment connects to any VR headset on the market and captures these eye movement patterns. • Analysis: the patterns are compared against our ML model to produce a risk analysis. Once classified, patients can access new interventions, such as the FDA-approved drugs. They're also referred to longevity practices, neurology practices or both, depending on their stage of decline. Testing for the earliest biomarkers allows the earliest possible intervention. In some cases, that slows the disease enough that patients outlive the onset of symptoms and never face memory loss in their lifetime.

**A big challenge?** You can prompt evidence chains to build conviction in external agents that your product creates real outcomes, has recurring users, and proper usage.

### Real-World RL Environments for Physical AI
We build real-world RL environments for robots. Starting with tasks from industry partners, we test policies on real robots and identify where they fail. We use those failures to decide what data to collect and curate for the next policy update. Next, we're setting up physical sandboxes at partner sites, so policies can train on the exact tasks and conditions they'll face in deployment.
Company Launches
SE3 Labs - Real-World RL Environments for Robot Models
See original launch post
**TL;DR:** **SE3 Labs** **builds real-world RL environments for robot models. We turn workflows from factories and hotels into repeatable tasks for training and evaluation, helping model teams move from capability to usability.**
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o5g-44iYAVY
Hi everyone! We're Mark, Conan and Paige, the team behind SE3 Labs.
**The problem**
Interactive environments and verifiable feedback have become important drivers of LLM post-training. Robot models need a similar learning loop in the physical world: attempt real tasks, learn from failures, and verify that improvements hold up beyond the lab.
But physical environments are much harder to scale than software environments. Every attempt requires a robot, a task setup, a reliable way to check success, and a reset before the next trial. This makes real-world evaluation costly and difficult to scale. Testing whether a robot can complete a benchmark task in the real world is already hard, let alone whether it can do useful work under deployment conditions.
**What we provide**
SE3 builds end-to-end real-world RL environments that move robot models from capability to usability. Think of it as a physical workbench where models can practice tasks that matter to end customers and receive feedback.
We help businesses to diagnose and improve robot learning policies. In return, they provide access to real workflows that we turn into repeatable tasks and RL environments. We handle site access, task setup, policy runs, human corrections, and resets.
We also work with model teams to define task verifiers: checks that determine whether a job was completed correctly and support reward signals for learning. Teams use failures to guide model updates, then test those updates on held-out variations.
**Example environments**
Our U.S. site network spans three types of environments and continues to expand:
- **Automotive & industrial facilities:** Assembly, insertion, and machine tending, with variations in parts, positioning, and tolerances.
- **Battery, recycling & food-processing facilities:** Environments for picking, sorting, and material handling.
- **Hotels & resorts:** Environments with real hospitality layouts, objects, and operating requirements.

### Next generation gas turbines for data centers & aviation
Viraj Aero builds gas turbines that deliver both power and cooling water for data centers. It needs no grid connection and no water pipeline. Burning natural gas already produces water. Our patented system captures that water from the exhaust. Part of it cools the data center. The rest is turned into steam and injected back into the turbine. That gives up to 40% more power from the same fuel (cheaper compute) and cuts NOx emissions by up to 99%, which cuts permit approvals from years to weeks. We're building a genset around our first-of-its-kind gas turbine. It fits in a 10-foot container and runs anywhere, even in the desert. That matters because two-thirds of new data centers are being built in water-stressed regions. We first built this steam-injected turbine for aircraft, where carrying water tanks isn't an option and efficiency is critical. We're currently integrating our full-scale prototype into an aircraft. The team comes from GE, Rolls-Royce and Formula 1, and we're already working with Safran, one of the world's largest aircraft engine manufacturers.

reific.text:
### RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time
Reific builds RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time, for the frontier labs that train agents. AI has learned to reason over text and code. But most of what matters in the real world shows up as numbers that change every second: a heartbeat, a gearbox, a GPU cluster. No human can track thousands of signals at once, but AI should be able to. In our environments, data streams in on a clock while the agent works, and every action is graded by what actually happened. Most AI training today teaches models to match human experts. We treat human performance as the floor. Each environment comes from real, de-identified records, in three task families: personal agents, industry, and science & compute. Today, even the best frontier model averages under 50% on each family. Training an open model on our environments raised its full-solve rate on unseen tasks by 54% (from 25.6% to 39.5%), with no loss on general benchmarks. Our mission is to build the infrastructure that keeps AI climbing the frontier, long past human level in the real world.

For decades, private credit origination has relied on relationships, because the market was fragmented and opaque. Someone had to know which fund was suitable for each specific deal, and coordinate a complex process to secure a term sheet. That knowledge lived in people's heads and inboxes, growing only based on headcount.
As agentic AI crosses the viability threshold, that expensive work is now free. When labor becomes abundant, two things become scarce instead. The former is lender attention. When submitting a deal costs nothing, lenders only review deals from sources they can trust. The latter is fluid knowledge on fund mandates. A live understanding of deals a lender is looking to fund.
Both are by-products of routing deals at scale. Forward is the private credit network for leading debt advisors. Advisors keep their borrowers and their fees. Lenders keep their credit judgment. We route the deals between them, and every deal we route sharpens our view of where capital will transact. That view is the foundation for the AI-native private credit fund we intend to build.

### Stripe for medical billing
Altair is an AI-native medical billing service for independent practices. We take over a practice's billing end to end and get doctors paid by insurers. AI does the work; our billers handle the exceptions. That can only work if a practice can trust an agent alone with its revenue. So we formalized insurers' billing policies and put a theorem prover under the agent. Before the agent acts on a claim, the prover checks the action against that insurer's policies, and anything that fails goes to one of our billers. Every claim teaches Altair how each insurer behaves, so the longer we run a practice's billing, the better we predict what its insurers will pay, deny or delay. We're building the default way a new practice gets paid: a doctor connects their EHR and bills clean, completely self-serve and on auto-pilot. Altair will be the financial platform every independent practice in America starts on and stays on. And to the Health Insurers' "Delay, Deny, Defend", we say "Predict, Prevent, Prevail".

### Continuous security verification for AI in regulated industries
Armorer helps companies in regulated industries ship their own AI systems faster and keep them secure in production. Most security tools flag an issue and file a ticket. Armorer assesses your agent and simulates attacks to find the real issues. Then it creates a verified fix that stops the attack without breaking the business, ready for your approval in about 4 hours. In production, Armorer checks every agent action in milliseconds, with no GPU needed. ### Maximize the AI you get from your Infrastructure
GPU capacity is sold like real estate: locked up, prepaid and idle half the time. Nodus makes it liquid, runs any AI workload on it through one execution layer, and puts research agents on every run to make the next one cheaper. More workloads mean better research, and better research means cheaper compute, a loop no single-product cloud can match.

**TL;DR:** The world is borrowing hundreds of billions of dollars to build GPUs, and the average GPU is busy 5% of the time. Nodus Compute gets more AI out of the GPUs that already exist. We fill idle hours with useful work, pack more models and jobs onto every card, and run training, RL, agents and inference on one platform.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P00rkHZenU8
### The AI buildout is running on debt
More than **$500 billion** of debt has gone into AI infrastructure (Forbes)). Data centers are financed against GPUs that lose value every year, on the bet that those GPUs stay busy.
They don't. Across tens of thousands of clusters, average GPU utilization was **5%** (Cast AI, 2026)).
Every idle hour is interest paid on hardware that produced nothing. The industry's answer is to borrow more and build more. Overclocking makes the car faster. Building more cars doesn't help either. **The seats are still empty.**
### The answer isn't more GPUs. It's more AI per GPU.
If the GPUs that already exist did twice the work, that would be like doubling the world's compute without another loan. That's the company we're building, and it's why we run our own research lab.
### Our research
Our lab works on one number: **useful AI per paid GPU-hour.** What we're working on:
- **Many models, fewer GPUs.** Serving lots of models from a shared pool of GPUs, instead of giving every model a GPU of its own.
- **Instant model switching.** Letting a GPU change the model it serves almost instantly, so no GPU has to sit reserved for one model.
- **Idle gaps become output.** Filling the quiet time behind live traffic with batch work, and running RL rollouts and training on the same GPUs.

👋 **Hey Everyone!** I'm Naman. My best friend Shubh and I are building **Antropi Robotics**.
**We make inspected CNC parts for hardware teams.** Our first factory is live and already shipping parts to customers with **lead times under 7 days**.
**Our goal:** a network of autonomous factories across the US, making and delivering parts locally in as little as 24 hours.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V4Ll5DZSP0I
## ⚙️ Problem
Before starting Antropi, I spent six months running my dad's CNC machining business in India. The biggest lesson was simple: **automating the machine is not the same as automating the factory.**
A CNC machine can cut automatically. But someone still has to plan the job, load the machine, inspect the part, and decide what to do when something goes wrong.
For hardware teams, this becomes a familiar cycle. Prepare drawings. Request quotes. Go back and forth on manufacturing details. Wait for a production slot. Wait for the parts.
**Every week spent waiting is a design iteration you don't get before your next demo.**
Adding a robot to load the machine fixes one step. It does not tell the factory whether the part is correct, or what should happen next.
## 🤖 Solution
We're building **dark factories: autonomous factories designed to run 24/7.** Our Factory OS connects job planning, CNC machines, robots, and inspection into one system.
Software turns CAD into machining programs and checks them in simulation, with an engineer approving them before production.
Robots load and unload. Machines cut. **Every part is inspected.**
Inspection feeds back into production, so the system can make supported corrections or stop the machine before a problem repeats.
uploaded image
For you, it's simple: upload your CAD, confirm your requirements, and receive inspected parts with an inspection report.
**You buy parts. We handle the factory.**
We're also building agent ordering through our MCP server and a **Rush option** for priority production.
uploaded image
## 🌎 Vision
**One factory is the start. The network is the point.**
Our long-term plan is hundreds, eventually thousands, of microfactories across the US, close to the teams building hardware. The same Factory OS will coordinate production across the network.
Autonomy removes waiting inside the factory. Local production puts the finished part closer

### The AI company brain for PE value creation
Plek is the AI company brain for private equity value creation. Upload an employee census, and Plek maps every person to a taxonomy of 50,000 jobs and 250,000 tasks, down to the time each task takes. It then analyzes spans and layers, org structure, footprint, compensation, functional fragmentation and AI exposure in parallel, and reconciles overlapping levers employee by employee so every dollar is traceable. What takes a performance improvement team 6 to 8 weeks takes Plek under a minute. At a 3,600-person company, Plek found $30M in annual EBITDA levers, matching what a global PE advisory firm found in six weeks. Funds and advisories use Plek from due diligence to exit to run org value creation scenarios, from the platform or from their own AI agents via MCP. Plek grew out of the MIT Work Analytics Lab, founded by CEO Pierre Bouquet during his MIT PhD. Long-term, Plek becomes the Celonis of the workforce: it continuously monitors the org and flags value creation levers as they appear.
