**TL;DR Underwater drones can navigate under the surface to reach ports, ships and seafloor cables, and no reliable solution exists to stop them. Caladh systems detect, track and defeat hostile drones by bringing the principles of electronic warfare underwater.** I'm **Kristen Kita**, founder of Caladh ("Call-luh"). I've spent the past decade working on this problem, starting with my PhD at MIT and most recently as a Principal Investigator for DARPA Sync. I started Caladh to close the gaps I've seen in how we protect critical infrastructure. https://youtu.be/oQJC\_hS07DQ
**What we do**
- **Eclipse: deny the drone.** Eclipse is a moored buoy that persistently protects ports, terminals, offshore energy sites and cable landings. It listens passively, and when a threat appears it triggers automatically or on an operator's command. It then denies the vehicle its navigation, comms and sensing both above and below the waterline, so the drone can't find its target or report back. A towed version deploys from a small boat for expeditionary missions. It's non-kinetic, unattended, and it plugs into existing C2 and layered defenses.
- **Cloak: hide the target.** Cloak sits low on the seabed next to cables, pipelines and other subsea assets. It defeats the imaging sonar and cameras that drones use to find and map those assets, so the asset blends back into the seafloor.

### Agents that engineer the grid edge
At least 94% of US outage minutes start on the distribution grid, and most utilities are blind between the substation and the meter. Evardi builds a live model of a utility's network from data it already has, matching every meter to its transformer and using virtual meters to show load and solar on every transformer. On top of that model, our AI agents do the engineering work utilities need at the grid edge: checking switching orders, finding outages after extreme weather and planning for new load from DERs and data centers. Because the model sees every transformer, it will also help utilities decide when new wires are really needed, and how distribution load can free up transmission for new data centers. We're working with utilities across the globe that together serve over 10 million customers.

### Enable enterprises to ship agent code without human review
Plover Labs is building toward a future where AI agents write, ship, and maintain most of a company's software. We make it possible for agents to own real engineering roles, not just suggest code for someone else to approve. Coding models keep getting more capable, but enterprise adoption lags behind AI-native startups because enterprises don't yet trust agent output. Each codebase has conventions, history, and failure modes that a general-purpose model doesn't know. We learn those continuously from the code, how the team works, and the mistakes agents make. Then we fix the codebase and add merge gates that use deterministic verifiers instead of another model's judgment, so the same mistake can't ship twice. As the gates build up, agents can be trusted with more of the work. We have five-figure monthly contracts with Series C companies Envoy and Fieldguide. At Fieldguide, we tripled PRs per engineer in one quarter, with the same headcount and PR size.

**For robots to be effective, they need to understand real world force and contact dynamics.**

Today's robotics companies and frontier physical AI model labs are spending **hundreds of millions** on egocentric video data to train their systems to perform tasks in place of humans. **Currently, there's no good way to get this data into a model.**
1. Tactile gloves occlude the user's hands.

routant.text:
### Last mile deployment and connectivity for Agents as a Service
AI agents won't stay inside the companies that build them. The most valuable agents will work across company boundaries, inside customers' private systems. In those environments, intelligence is no longer the barrier to deployment. Trust and access are. Routant is the zero-trust access layer for this new agentic world. Vendors integrate once, while customers retain governance over every deployment, deciding what agents can access and which actions need human review, with a complete audit trail of every action.
Company Launches
Routant - Let AI agents into your apps, on your rules
See original launch post
**TL;DR**
Routant lets AI agents work inside your apps and private systems, with access rules you control. Choose which tools an agent can use, require approval for sensitive actions, and review what it did.
https://youtu.be/3cYCNFWQjuc
**The Problem**
An AI agent is only useful if it can get into the systems where the work happens: your inbox, your database, your payment provider, a customer's internal tools. Today, giving it that access is all or nothing.
An agent connected to your email can read messages it has no reason to see. An IT agent troubleshooting a production issue may need access to infrastructure far beyond the affected system. And a company deploying support agents across customers needs to navigate a different set of private networks, credentials, and security policies for every environment.
Teams stitch together VPNs, custom integrations, credentials, and approval workflows to make this work. They often rely on prompt instructions or scattered configuration files to limit what agents can do, but these aren't reliable security boundaries. The result is that agents either get too much access, creating unnecessary risk, or too little, leaving humans to do the work themselves.
**Our Solution**
Routant sits between your agents and the systems they use, and enforces your rules on every request.
- Connect once: agents reach your apps through a single MCP endpoint. Private and on-prem systems connect through an outbound-only gateway, with no inbound ports to open.
- Selective access: an agent only sees the tools and data you've granted. For example, your assistant can handle work email while messages from friends stay invisible to it.
- Approvals for what matters: sensitive actions are held until someone approves them, and disallowed actions are blocked outright.
- A full record: every request and decision is logged, so you can see exactly what the agent did.
Because the rules live in Routant and are built into the access itself, they hold no matter what the prompt says. For companies building agents, each customer sets its own rules, so you integrate once instead of rebuildi

Hi everyone! We're Daniel and Krish, the founders of Vorelios.
**TL;DR:** Vorelios is a research lab building AI that can engineer anything. Our model takes a design's geometry and predicts its fluid, thermal, and structural behavior in seconds instead of hours or days of simulation, and uses those predictions to invent and improve designs autonomously. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7\_CMTf\_Z-SE
**The problem**
We already understand the physics behind many of the technologies we want to build. But knowing the equations doesn't give us a working design. Computing how a single design will behave can take hours or days of simulation, and finding one that works means investigating many possibilities. That process can take years, so we only explore a small fraction of what could work.
AI can explain the physics and propose designs, but evaluating those designs still depends on the same expensive simulations. Most AI for simulation today trains a separate model for each problem and only works on designs close to what it was trained on. We're building one model that learns how physics actually works, so it can predict how completely new designs will behave and use those predictions to engineer them.

- **It works from CAD.** Give it clean geometry and operating conditions, and it predicts the full physical fields in a fraction of a second.

**What enforcement looks like today**
Chris and I found ourselves frustrated by the deluge of undisclosed advertising on social media (which violates FTC guidelines) and started thinking,"How does a government agency capture the true scope of illicit activity at scale?"
That question led us to find that most consumer protection regulation today still starts with a complaint. Investigators work through an inbox that never empties, while millions of websites change every day. Most people who are harmed never file at all.
The result is ad hoc enforcement: few companies get caught and often years later. When breaking the rules rarely costs anything, competition stops being about who builds the better product and starts being about who's willing to cheat.
**What Particularity does**

- **Investigate.** Every complaint gets a first-pass investigation within the same minute, matched against evidence already on file.
- **Act.** Findings map to the elements of the law, so staff can move straight to a warning letter or enforcement action.

### Automated post-training for LLMs
Latent automates post-training for LLMs. It reads signals inside a model as it works and labels every answer and agent step in milliseconds, so teams improve their models on their own production traffic instead of paying for human labeling. The same signal works in real time. Latent lets an output through, holds it, re-asks a stronger model, or sends it to review with the reason attached. Reading the model is over 660x cheaper than running an LLM judge, so it can check everything. One voice AI company using Latent finds 98% of its agent's failures by reviewing only the riskiest 43% of answers, and in testing Latent stopped 99% of rule-breaking agents before they acted, against 69% for a frontier LLM judge. It works with self-hosted and API models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini, runs hosted or fully in your own cloud, and installs with one line of code.

**The Problem:**
Every team running AI wants its model to get more accurate, and that takes labeled data from its own production traffic. Today that means paying experts by the hour or running an LLM judge on every answer, which is slow and expensive. So most teams label a small sample, ship everything else unchecked, and lose the signal in the rest.
AI also fails quietly. A model gives a confident answer that's wrong, like the wrong dosage or a refund policy that doesn't exist. An agent takes a shortcut it was told not to take. The dashboard is green and last week's evals passed. You find out when a customer does. As agents run longer with no one watching, that gap gets wider.
**What We're Doing:**
**1. Labeling every answer by reading the model.** Latent scores every answer and agent step from signals inside the model, at over 660x lower cost than an LLM judge. On self-hosted models it adds no latency. On API models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini, a lightweight reader scores each answer in milliseconds. Each label comes with the failure type and the riskiest sentence.

### Electrifying North American freight rail with swappable batteries.
Ailit is building the electric energy system for North American freight rail. Our first product, Superwagon, is a battery wagon designed to power existing diesel-electric locomotives, allowing railroads to electrify the fleets they already own. Superwagon carries swappable battery packs that supply electricity to the locomotive's existing electric motors. Discharged packs are exchanged for charged ones along the route and recharged off-board, providing operators with limitless range. We deliver energy as a service, owning and operating the batteries and swapping sites. Railroads pay for energy with no upfront equipment purchase, with pricing set at 20% below today's diesel cost. Founded in Stockholm by Christian Lind and Emil Tagesson, our team is now based in San Francisco. We're building our first full-scale prototype, and it's being prepared to move a locomotive on battery power in the coming days.

### CI runner with agents that manage your tests. 10x faster and 70%...
Graphide CI runs your CI 10× faster than GitHub runners on enterprise deployments, and our 24/7 agents optimize the CI itself, not just the machines. We cut costs 70%+ for GH (50%+ for most other runners) and take over the ongoing work of optimizing CI, so you can focus on your product. We're faster and cheaper because we own both the hardware and the optimizations and configs that run on it, which lets us do what owning only one could not. A graph of the codebase runs only the tests each change can reach, and we run your tests in parallel, so your CI is limited only by the length of your longest test. Our agents then tune machines, caches and test splits as you add more tests and code over time. We also patch the tests themselves, fixing flakes and adding our own libraries so they run faster and more reliably. Coding agents now write more code than teams can check, making verification the new bottleneck. CI is where we start, but we also cover the rest of the verification stack. Our PR review agent runs the old and new code in live environments, finding bugs and proving them by writing tests (50% more bugs found than Greptile on our benchmarks, with 35% fewer false positives). Our visualizer shows data flows and graph-based diffs so you can understand a PR in seconds.

Hi! We are Alper and Samriddhi, co-founders at Odin Robotics.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K-Mein4nAlA
**Why the work stays manual**
Traditional automation means rebuilding the factory around the robot. It's built for one product running the same way millions of times. Most factories don't work like that. They run many products, change over often, and handle parts that never show up exactly the same way twice. Robots that only follow a fixed program break the moment anything changes, so the work stays manual.
**What's in the demos**
- **Machine tending:** fully automated tending of a CNC mill. The robot loads raw parts, runs the cycle and unloads finished parts, with no operator needed.
- **Conveyor packing:** food containers picked off a moving conveyor and packed into totes in real time.
**Our approach**
The best software combines deterministic code, trained models, and LLMs. Robotics is no different. Programmed controls run the steps that must be exact every time: machine doors, fixtures, safety zones. Learned skills handle everything that varies: new parts, mixed products, cluttered bins, and items that are soft or irregular. Our robots don't need every part perfectly placed. kanopy.text:
### Computer vision operating layer for physical infrastructure
Video to automatically identify risks and condition on power lines, pipelines, rail, and other types of infrastructure over hundreds of miles at once.
Company Launches
Kanopy - spatial intelligence for physical infrastructure
See original launch post
TL;DR: Utilities plan operations using field data that can be years out of date. Kanopy uses computer vision to turn ordinary video into a 3D model of the grid, helping teams map tree risks, assess asset condition, and plan maintenance. We've already deployed across thousands of miles of power lines.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VFx7\_ZF07nI
**The problem**
There are roughly 100 million miles of above-ground linear infrastructure worldwide. The electricity grid alone accounts for ~60 million miles (equivalent to 2,500 times around the equator). Infrastructure is aging, the cost of failure is higher than ever, and the systems we rely on are too vast to monitor manually.
For utilities, vegetation management makes this challenge concrete. Arborists patrol power lines to identify dangerous trees and determine what needs cutting. Contractors estimate the work using manual surveys and historical averages. Once crews finish trimming, utilities send people back to verify the work.
Planning the work and executing these multiple inspections take millions in spent resources.
**What Kanopy does**
Kanopy turns ordinary video from any camera into a detailed 3D model of the grid. The video can come from a drone, a GoPro on a truck, or simply from an iPhone shot.
Our models measure vegetation clearances, identifies hazards, and assesses asset condition. Utilities use these insights to prioritize maintenance, plan fieldwork, and verify completed work. Each new drive or flight can refresh that picture using cameras teams already own.
uploaded image
**The team**

### Marketplace for AI inference: the right model at the best price
RouterPlus is a marketplace for AI inference. We find the right AI model for a team's product, then get it served at the team's scale, at the best price. Most teams that run AI in production pay for a top model on every task, when a cheaper model can do most of the work. The same model can also cost twice as much depending on which provider runs it, and many providers fail at peak traffic. RouterPlus tests models on a team's own traffic and recommends one. Providers then compete for the workload. We check that the chosen provider can hold the team's real peak, and we keep a second provider ready as a backup. Teams call the model through one API. Our largest customer runs 3 million agent conversations a day on RouterPlus.

Coding agents have made building cheap. Checking has not kept up. Teams tell us about features that pass CI and get approved by a review bot, then fail the first time a real person tries them. Memorable: graph procedural memory for AI agents. Stop re-teaching your agents!
See original launch post
# | TL;DR: Memorable records the tool calls an agent made to run a task, reuses that workflow on similar tasks instead of re-deriving through reasoning from scratch. -60% tool calls, -40% latency.
https://youtu.be/3m9I1zHSMPk
**Memorable turns agent reasoning into a graph search problem.**
1. We **capture your agents' traces** and store them as a lightweight graph.
2. When a similar prompt arrives, we **extrapolate a workflow with a graph search.**
3. We **inject a short pointer** (50 to 100 tokens) into the prompt.
uploaded image
# **So the agent runs deterministically instead of re-deriving a plan every. single. time.**

caveman.text:
### Infrastructure for efficient AI
Caveman is the cheapest place to build and run AI agents. It observes real agent workloads, finds cost and performance inefficiencies, tests improvements, and safely deploys the ones that work.
Company Launches
Caveman (F26) is building the cloud for AI agents
See original launch post
Hey everyone, I'm Julius, founder of Caveman. **Caveman gives developers the primitives to build and deploy production agents that get more work done per dollar of compute.** We recently actually hit 5 trillion tokens a week flowing through our platform.
When an agent reads a file, calls a model, or spins up a machine, those decisions determine what the task costs. Caveman controls all three. We can see where a real workload wastes time and compute, test changes against the tasks the agent actually has to complete, and ship the ones that lower cost while keeping quality up.
**So what can you actually build on Caveman?**
Build an agent with our SDK and deploy it on Caveman Cloud with zero-clicks (just ask your agent lol). The runtime decides what context to carry forward so the model spends fewer tokens rereading the same data. It can pick a model for each step and provision a cloud machine with the tools the agent needs, then shut it down when the work is done.
Then if you want to evaluate how your agent actually works before production, use our eval-suite. Or if you decide you don't want to manually A/B test every model, same answer.
Those primitives work together. If a task gets expensive, you can change what the agent reads, which model it calls, or how it runs, then rerun the workload and see what happened to the **cost per successful task**.
**How this started**
Seven months ago, my AI bill was bigger than my grocery bill. I was a uni student, so mostly as a joke I wrote a Markdown file that made Claude talk like a caveman. "Why use many token when few do trick." Someone I'd never met posted it on Hacker News. It hit #1, and 120,000 GitHub stars later, it's my full-time job.
When I measured longer agent workloads on Opus 5.5, what the agent wrote accounted for less than a tenth of the cost. A big part of the bill came from what the agent had to read again at every step. That's what got me building the infrastructure underneath it.
**Try the stack in Caveman Code**
Caveman Code is our Mac and browser app built on Caveman Cloud. Give Chief a task and it can coordinate multiple agents and report back. Agents can use a cloud desktop or browser to check their work and, in beta, keep running when you close your laptop. Watch the demo
**Same models, more work per dollar**

Star us on Github! https://github.com/TerseAI/durable-actors Durable Actors help you build real-time applications like chat systems (e.g. ChatGPT, Codex), collaboration tools (e.g. Notion), and agent swarms (e.g. Devin).
They provide *stateful serverless functions*, a foundational building block that abstracts away persistence, coordination, and infrastructure challenges in distributed systems.
Why is this useful? It reduces complexity tremendously and It saves you a lot of money!
Our actors go dormant and back up in S3 when not in use. So agents only incur cost when your users are getting value from them. Because each actor has its own database and websocket server, we remove a ton of pressure from your main DB as well as your websocket server and you can scale those down.
In addition to being cost efficient, they are the perfect tool for building agentic applications. You no longer need to store JSONB in your Postgres DB, no more complicated websocket logic, it handles race conditions elegantly and helps keeps your REST API fully stateless.

We're Aarush & Arnav - co-founders of The Subvocal Company
TL;DR: We're building glasses that let you talk to your computer without talking out loud. You mouth the words silently, and almost invisibly, and Subvocal decodes it to text in real time.
Edit: Since launch, we've received roughly 750 paid preorders and collected about $150,000 in refundable deposits. The launch video reached more than 12 million views on X. We've also miniaturized the prototype into more comfortable, portable glasses and are getting ready to ship it out to our first customers in a few months.

**Why we're building this**
Voice is the fastest, most natural way to use a computer and as agents handle more work, our job moves upstream, to structured and detailed prompting. Expressing your thoughts is best done through unconstrained, open voice. Wispr Flow's popularity has shown how much people love fast input.
But voice also fails in exactly the moments it needs to work. In an open office or a cafe or in public transit, it's incredibly awkward for you and distracting for those around you to talk into your computer.
People have found incredibly creative and weird workarounds to this, including gooseneck whisper mics and even sound proof masks you can talk into.
We wanted the speed of speech without having to make a sound.
**How it works**
Subvocal uses RF sensing from a pair of glasses to pick up the tiny facial movements you make while silently articulating words.
We send low-power radio waves through the face and measure how they change as your muscles move. Our models then decode those signals directly into text.
You can articulate clearly, or do it subtly enough that someone sitting across from you barely notices.

tl;dr: Tilion is the fastest and stealthiest browser infrastructure in the world. Type "setup tilion.com" into your agent and it can go anywhere on the web.
The internet is the best thing we have built. Most of what humanity knows sits on it, and anyone can walk in. Agents can now use it too, and the web treats them as second-class. Every agent works for a person, so whatever the web keeps from an agent it keeps from that person.
uploaded image
**The problem**
To do anything on the web, an agent needs a browser. Most sites worth visiting sit behind Cloudflare, DataDome, Akamai or a CAPTCHA, and those systems can't tell your agent from a scraper. The agent gets a block page, reads it as if it were the content, and the task fails without anyone noticing.
Teams building agents fight this themselves. They rent proxies, solve CAPTCHAs, patch fingerprints, and redo all of it every time a site changes. Scaling is another big problem all together.
https://youtu.be/V2NlqvpqpzQ
**Why nobody had fixed it**
Getting through is stealth, and getting through fast is speed. Browser providers pick one, because stealth is paid for in time: real browsers, warm profiles, residential IPs, waiting out challenges. Speed comes from deleting all of that, which is exactly what bot detection looks for.
An agent runs in a loop, twenty page loads for one task, with a person waiting at the end. It needs both.
**What we built**
Tilion runs on Fortress, our open-source build of Chromium. We fix the fingerprint inside the browser's C++, so there is no script layer for a site to detect. Fortress has 200,000+ installs.

The Agentic Data Company - Real-world speech data and RL environments for speech models
See original launch post
#### TL;DR
We design and collect datasets of how people actually speak in real life, and we build RL environments so speech models can sound and act human. Our open-source dataset has been the #1 audio dataset on Hugging Face for about 2 months, and the turn-taking model we trained on it ranks #1 on Sesame's TurnBench.
**Ask:** Building a foundational speech model? We'd love to meet you: matias@theagenticdatacompany.com
https://youtu.be/oLP84ur80Zk
#### The problem
Speech models have made huge progress in the last year, but conversations still feel robotic, and the models break down on real-world agentic tasks. A model is only as good as its data, and speech data mostly can't be scraped or generated synthetically. Humans have to create it. Today that means gig workers, which works for grading code or math. But how people speak depends entirely on the setting: a support call sounds nothing like talking to a friend. Data alone also won't get speech models to the next level. Code and text models improved by training in RL environments, and speech models need the same thing.
#### What we do
- **Real-world speech datasets:** We build everyday apps that plug into conversations people already have and record them with clear consent. That gives us real speech in real environments, at a fraction of the cost of gig-based vendors.
- **Audio-native RL environments:** We build RL environments for speech where models train on agentic tasks, perception, dialogue and tool use all at once, with no human in the loop. Imagine worlds for airlines, hotels, personal agents, and much more.
#### Team
Matias and Christian met 7 years ago working in London. They've been friends ever since. Christian founded and sold his last company, Postbuddy. Matias built data science and the growth engine at Female Invest (YC S21), which grew to 1M women and 85K paying members. Named one of Denmark's top 20 marketing talents by M Talent.

graypass.text:
### Verify the expected person is still in control before sensitive...
Login tells you who signed in. GrayPass helps apps check who's behind sensitive actions and whether they're authorized before those actions go through. It combines identity, device and session context with behavioral signals like typing rhythm, cursor movement and scrolling. Before a sensitive action goes through, GrayPass evaluates that evidence against your team's policy and returns a decision: allow, challenge, hold or deny. Your app enforces the decision. This applies to actions like exporting sensitive data, changing admin permissions or allowing an AI agent to act on someone's behalf. Allowed actions receive short-lived, signed proof tied to the exact action and your app. Your existing login and authentication stack stays in place.

tilo.title: Public page
tilo.text:
### The Microsoft of the AI era: the operating system for AI agents.
Tilo gives AI agents one shared computer. Today every agent gets its own virtual machine and works by screenshots and clicks, which is slow, expensive and brittle. Agents that work together have to describe what they did to each other in messages. Tilo is a Linux-based operating system built for agents as users. Every app exports typed actions that agents call over MCP while people use the same actions as buttons, on the same live state. Many agents work in one workspace at once and read each other's work instead of messaging about it. Every change is attributed and can be undone, and irreversible actions need permission. Because state and interface are separate, agents can generate an app's entire UI on demand. On the same multi-app task with the same model, agents on Tilo were about 29× cheaper and 90× faster than computer use, which failed. A small model on Tilo did it for about 1/10,000 of the frontier model's cost. In our scale test, 50 agents worked in one shared workspace on a single laptop, at about 60 MB of memory per agent. Tilo runs headless, in our cloud, or as a desktop, and you can open any workspace from the browser.

superserve.title: Public page
superserve.text:
### Virtual machines for long-running agents
Superserve gives every AI agent its own computer in the cloud. Each one is an isolated VM that starts in under 50ms, sleeps between turns, and picks up exactly where it left off, for hours, weeks or indefinitely. Traditional cloud infrastructure was built to run one app for many users. Agents flip that. Each agent needs its own isolated machine where it can write and run code, use tools and work on its own for long stretches. Everything it produces has to persist the whole time, the way your laptop keeps your work. That means agent computers have to be stateful, secure and cheap to run. For agents that talk to customers, they also have to start, sleep and wake almost instantly. Fast - Machines start in under 50ms, either cold or from a template with your repo and dependencies already loaded. You don't need to keep a pool of servers running and waiting. Persistent - Paused machines keep their full memory and disk state at zero compute cost. They can resume or fork from that exact state. Pausing and resuming is fast enough that a machine can sleep between inference calls and wake on the next turn. Agents can run Docker, databases, browsers or any other service inside. Secure - Every machine is a microVM with its own kernel. You can program the rules for what traffic can come in and go out, and they're enforced at the network boundary where the agent can't reach them. API secrets are handled at the network layer too, so they never enter the machine. Every action is logged for audits. Teams building coding agents, autonomous workers, and eval or RL training environments use Superserve to give every agent session or rollout its own machine, with no infrastructure to manage. We run 100K+ machines every week for teams including Lindy and Y Combinator.

hundred.text:
### 100% automated inspection for precision hardware parts
Hundred is an automated inspection system for the components that make up devices like phones, smartwatches, and laptops. Hundred helps factories cut waste and prevent line-down issues by catching sub-100µm visual defects before parts reach the assembly line. Designs change so fast that traditional machine vision can't keep up, forcing factories to rely on manual inspection, literally people checking parts under microscopes to sort out bad parts. Human inspectors miss roughly 15% of defects, and a single bad part can turn a finished device into scrap. Hundred is replacing manual inspection with an imaging rig that scans an entire shipping tray of parts at once. The Hundred rig blocks ambient light and uses varied controlled lighting configurations to detect defects smaller than 100µm on a range of materials. The controlled environment means Hundred only needs to scan a single good part before it can find defects, categorize them, and assess their severity accurately. Defects cost U.S. discrete manufacturers $45 billion a year, a problem Hundred's CEO, Erica, saw firsthand as a mechanical engineer designing devices at Meta, Google, and Magic Leap. She met Imani, Hundred's CPO, at Columbia University's admitted-students day in 2017 and Imani went on to spend five years at Twitch building software that handles billions of requests a day. Erica later met Iris, Hundred's CTO, in the Bay Area. Iris worked as a quant at Citadel before pivoting to study at Imperial College London where she researched machine learning on 3D meshes and other structured data. Together, they're building Hundred because manual inspection shouldn't still exist in 2026.

None of these were caught by code review or traditional scanners.

OpenHack built a custom harness refined over months. **TL;DR:** Every healthcare transaction should be paid according to the contract. Today, billions aren't. Cesara reads a health system's payer contracts and checks every claim against them when it's submitted. When a payment comes back short, Cesara automatically files the appeal with the contract clause attached and recovers the money. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IDbQo3WsSGY
### The problem: contracts change, but team capacity doesn't
Payer contracts keep changing. Amendments, fee schedule updates and annual rate increases all change what a hospital should be paid partway through the year. Every change has to be loaded and checked by hand. Revenue cycle and managed care teams can't keep up, so underpayments only show up months later in spreadsheets, after the payment has posted. **Health systems lose $40B+ a year from contractual underpayments.**
### How Cesara works
- **Every contract in one place.** Cesara pulls rates, carve-outs, stop-loss terms and rate increases from the contracts themselves. It keeps them in sync with Epic, your contract management system, SharePoint, payer email and your chargemaster.
- **Every claim checked when it's submitted.** Cesara calculates the expected payment up front. Say a payer pays $42,000 on a claim where the contract's stop-loss clause means $78,000 is owed. Your team sees the gap right away, with the clause attached.
- **Automatic recovery.** Cesara files each appeal with the contract excerpt and the payer's remittance (835) attached. It tracks the appeal until the money is recovered and the claim is closed.
- **Better contract negotiations.** Your team can ask its contracts anything in plain language and model proposed rates before signing. They walk into payer meetings with payment trends and evidence ready.

### Defense compliant modular battery packs power systems and vehicles
We started off building the highest performance, 470 volt electric off-road vehicles but we realized our ultra power dense battery packs are useful for mobile and stationary energy storage and power export, for military and consumer use cases. We develop battery packs, power electronics, and traction powertrain systems for vehicles. Our tech is so compelling because the safety and layout of high voltage battery packs has only been mastered by large, well funded OEM companies who have brought it in-house. flashdrive.text:
### A shared drive for your team and all your AI agents.
Our mission is to rebuild the file system, the oldest idea in computing, for its newest users: AI agents. FlashDrive is a shared drive for teams and their AI agents. You can use it via MCP or mount it like a normal folder on macOS and Linux, so your laptop, your teammates' and every sandbox work in the same live files at once. Agents hand off work through files: one writes, the next one reads. That makes AI multiplayer across a whole company. Everyone keeps the agent they already like, whether that's Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or something custom, and there's no new app to learn. Your agents and your teammates' agents work in the same files and pick up where each other left off. Shared drives were built for people. Agents work differently: many of them edit the same files at once. Unlike Dropbox or Google Drive, FlashDrive merges edits made at the same time, or keeps both, instead of creating a conflicted copy. Cloud sandboxes connect with no setup, huge files stream instead of filling the disk, and every file can be searched with keywords and grep. (FlashDrive is by Evokoa, Inc.)

DeepMark is the authentication layer for AI voice. When an AI agent speaks, we embed a compact, machine-readable ID directly into the audio, not in metadata, which gets stripped the moment a file is touched. Voice is uniquely vulnerable to impersonation. spacesheep.text:
### Documents of the future: the collaboration surface for people and...
Agents now write faster than anyone can read. Spacesheep is where their work lands: any agent turns a session's output into a space that your team takes in at a glance. It works with the agents you already use, and has its own agent built in. Teams work on it together: comment on the exact spot, @mention a teammate, or ask @spacesheep and an agent makes the change live on every screen. Every change is a version, and every space is searchable by meaning, for people and agents alike. Spaces can show live data streamed from servers and sensors, and connect to the tools your team already uses. Teams use it for research, design docs, dashboards, slides and internal apps.

Hey everyone, I'm Michael, the founder of Spacesheep (F26).
## TL;DR
**Spacesheep: documents of the future.** Spaces are the place your teams and agents can be productive. Your AI makes the space; your team reads it, comments on it and builds on it.
Ask the AI you already use: "Use spacesheep.dev and give a visual explanation of how GPUs work." You get a document, a mockup, a dashboard, an app or art. Share it with specific people, your team, or publicly.
Our launch video:
https://youtu.be/cFVCDSs-GZs
Agents make our work more productive. Their output keeps growing, but our ability to read stays the same. We're building a new surface where people understand and work with AI.
Spacesheep in 90 seconds:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vKQtOTrRBBA
## Why we're building it
Agent use pushes productivity, but we get constantly burned out by relentless walls of AI-generated text. We don't believe a chat interface is the final evolution of human-computer interaction. Agents know how to shape information for humans, and that shape is not a wall of text. The full story: spacesheep.dev/why
## What we built
If you can imagine it, you can sheep it. Information can take many more shapes than a page. With one prompt, create and share designs, styled documents, dashboards and vibe-coded apps your team and customers work in together.

### Applied AI for Enterprise GTM (3x founders, 10x growth, backed by ANT)
Gather's AI agent for enterprise GTM continually interviews real buyers and turns those conversations into content that drives pipeline and simulations that predict customer behavior. More than 65 enterprise marketing teams, including Envoy, Eclypsium, Cover Genius, Fortinet, CoStar, Bagel Brands, and Family Express, use Gather to create original, on-brand, third-party validated thought leadership, reports, ebooks, and campaign content. Teams can simulate how buyers will respond to messaging, pricing, and market shifts, with supporting evidence and a confidence level behind every answer. When confidence is low, Gather automatically runs new research. We're starting by replacing research firms and content agencies. luminary.title: Public page
luminary.text:
### AI CEO that leads human & agent teams on company-wide missions
Luminary is an AI CEO that leads human and agent teams on company-wide missions. We're building the complete infrastructure for a fully AI-native company, starting with a world model of how your business works and building up to an AI CEO that can lead it. Today's AI tools are good at automating the work they're handed, but they still wait to be told what to do next. So even with the abundance of AI agents, companies are still bottlenecked by leadership and vision. Someone has to decide what's worth building, rally the right people behind it, and bring it to market. Luminary takes on that job. Instead of asking it to build a feature, you hand it part of your business to grow. It then proactively discovers opportunities, plans high-impact missions, and leads your people and its own agent swarms to accomplish them. Some examples of audacious missions it can execute: - Launch a product: It spots customers building the same workaround, makes the business case, directs coding agents to build it, and rolls it out. - Enter a new market: It finds an unexpected group of buyers, reworks positioning and pricing around them, and wins the first accounts. - Rescue a stalled deal: It notices an enterprise deal losing momentum, designs a new strategy with your sales team, and gets it signed. Under the hood, Luminary builds a living world model and follows a leadership constitution that shapes every call. Proprietary evals check every deliverable, and a recursive self-improvement loop turns each mission into institutional wisdom.

### Robotics workforce for hotels
Vibe Robotics builds robots for the work nobody should have to repeat. We're starting in hotels. Every day, housekeeping teams move linens between floors, restock carts, and fold stacks of laundry before the next guests arrive. It's physical work that has to get done every shift. Our first robot, Vibe 01, folds a hand towel fully autonomously in 23.8 seconds. It learned from just a few hundred human demonstrations. We're piloting Vibe 01 at a Hilton property and working with hotels under the Marriott, Hilton, and IHG brands to bring it to more locations. Folding is the first job. Next are restocking housekeeping carts and moving linens between floors. We're Archer, Daniel, Katherine, and Pranav, and we're building robots that can learn to do routine physical work across industries.

Message from Dan Siroker, Co-Founder & CEO
I'm excited to share that Limitless has been acquired by Meta. I'm going to share why we joined forces, what this means for customers, and what comes next.
First, why? When we started Limitless five years ago, the world was very different. AI was a pipe dream to many. Hardware startups were considered unfundable, and a business that did both AI and hardware would have been considered ludicrous.
But today is different. The world has changed. We're no longer working on a weird fringe idea. We're building a future that now seems inevitable. We're not alone.
Meta recently announced a new vision to bring personal superintelligence to everyone and a key part of that vision is building incredible AI-enabled wearables. We share this vision and we'll be joining Meta to help bring our shared vision to life.
What does this mean for existing customers? Good news. We will continue to support existing Pendant customers for at least another year, but we'll no longer sell the Pendant to new customers. You'll no longer need to pay a subscription, and existing customers get the Unlimited Plan for free. That said, we will be sunsetting non-Pendant functionality like Rewind, and there'll be updates to regional availability. For continuing customers, you will need to agree to our updated Privacy Policy and Terms of Service. Whether you choose to continue to use the Pendant or not, your data will remain safe.
We just launched a feature to make it easy to export all of your data. And of course, if you want to delete all of your data, that is also very easy to do within the app.
Lastly, I want to thank each and every one of you for going on this journey with us. I look forward to sharing more when I can.
Thanks,

OUR APPROACH
### We are deliberately anti-thematic
Only a small handful of companies grow into tomorrow's winners. Nearly all sit in new market categories that aren't obvious at the time. We've trained ourselves to write the check when we think we come across a founder building something of significance.
### Our companies want to win the US market
We encourage our companies to not waste time and tackle the US market early. Our 50+ years combined tenure in Silicon Valley lets us access senior relationships that would ordinarily be challenging to reach.

We invest early in brilliant people and products and care more about the potential of massive scale and less about minimizing risk in a company's early days. Our business is about maximizing upside, not protecting downside.

###### **Due to the potential for losses, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) considers this investment to be high risk!**
**What are the key risks?**
**1. You could lose all the money you invest**
If the business you invest in fails, you are likely to lose 100% of the money you invested. Most start-up businesses fail.
**2. You are unlikely to be protected if something goes wrong**
The business offering this investment is not regulated by the FCA. Protection from the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) only considers claims against failed regulated firms. Learn more about FSCS protection **here**.
Protection from the Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS) does not cover poor investment performance. If you have a complaint against an FCA-regulated firm, FOS may be able to consider it. Learn more about FOS protection **here**.
**3. You won't get your money back quickly**
Even if the business you invest in is successful, it may take several years to get your money back. You are unlikely to be able to sell your investment early. The most likely way to get your money back is if the business is bought by another business or lists its shares on an exchange such as the London Stock Exchange. These events are not common. If you are investing in a start-up business, you should not expect to get your money back through dividends. Start-up businesses rarely pay these.
**4. Don't put all your eggs in one basket**
Putting all your money into a single business or type of investment, for example, is risky. Spreading your money across different investments makes you less dependent on anyone to do well. A good rule of thumb is not to invest more than 10% of your money in **high-risk investments.** Read more about it **here**.
**5. The value of your investment can be reduced**
The percentage of the business that you own will decrease if the business issues more shares. This could mean that the value of your investment reduces, depending on how much the business grows. Most start-up businesses issue multiple rounds of shares. These new shares could have additional rights that your shares don't have, such as the right to receive a fixed dividend, which could further reduce your chances of getting a return on your investment. If you are interested in learning more about how to protect yourself, visit the FCA's website **here**.

## Principles
**Investing sweat, reputation and (our own) capital.** To support you in building the startup you want on your tombstone, not just your social media bio.
**Fully aligned with your business model, not ours.** We've been successful enough investing other people's money that now we're using our own. An angel's flexibility with institutional experience. No BS advice. Help navigating fundraising and other key moments.
**Increasing the probability, velocity, and scale of your success.** We earn your trust to be both reactive and proactive partners. We provide a 24 hour SLA on any urgent need - closing a hire, vetting an investor, navigating a critical negotiation.
## Seeking
**Conviction** You're building with love in your heart and a key insight in your head. You also have a chip on your shoulder to solve a problem you know intimately. And you have a keen vision for the world that needs to exist to solve it.
**Commitment** You understand that startups require sacrifice at times. You know that an insatiable desire to learn, to bring others along with you and to win are necessary but not sufficient. You appreciate that commitment doesn't mean sacrificing family, health or ethics.
**LUV** The problem you're trying to solve is **L**arge, **U**rgent, and **V**aluable. You believe that technology can transform industries and unleash new markets, improving access and opportunity for everyone.
## Investing
**Early** 90% of what we do is pre-seed/seed investments of between $100k and $500k. 10% is larger (up to $25+ million) and/or later.
**Flexible** No ownership targets - we can be the first check, last check, or anywhere in-between.
**Focused** Your startup is located in North or South America and initially targets markets in those geographies

# what's with the dog?
In 2008, Spark led Twitter's Series B and made a very dear friend in the process, Twitter's Co-Founder, Biz Stone.
Over the years, we remained very close. And in 2017, after selling Jelly to Pinterest, Biz decided to think about his next move while working out of Spark's San Francisco office.
At the same time, Spark was also thinking about its next move, but as a brand. Biz, having worked with us for over a decade, saw an answer for Spark and made us this deck. We loved it. His wit and unbound creativity makes us smile to this day. But as branding goes in venture (hint: it doesn't go), the deck got tucked away.
In 2020, we decided to take a fresh look at Spark's identity. This meant going through our archives and delivering the full digital pile-including Biz's deck-to our design partner, Pentagram.
As we explored Spark's values, beliefs, and how we show up for our founders, Biz's work finally clicked (not to mention, he has a track record with animal-based logos).
Pentagram decided to revisit that deck and rework those sketches. And, well, Biz-you were right. A dog is spot-on.

## We started Vertex US from a desire to pay it forward
We saw the positive impact of high-conviction and highly present investors when we were building our companies, so we founded Vertex US to do the same.
Our special power is partnering with technical founders to nail the go-to-market and assemble exceptional teams. We'll share lessons learned from our journeys as company builders and bring curiosity and candor to every step.
- "I remember meeting Vertex for the first time[...] I instantly felt a bit more comfortable because they were founders, and so I didn't feel like I had to put on a suit and tie and do the investor dance. I felt like I could talk about product, I could talk about the value that we're bringing to our customers and even ask questions, get mentored. I think that was what made me choose Vertex at the end of the day when we had multiple term sheets. There's a lot of money in Silicon Valley, but former founders who've seen the movie once or twice, and then seen it at the scale that the Vertex team has seen it, is very rare. " Jerry Ting, cofounder of Evisort (acq. Workday, 2024)
- "[The] thing that impresses me about Vertex is this: The fact that you're doing all these extra things to amplify the message, amplify the position of the portfolio companies, helping us with recruiting great talent to join our team and connecting us with potential customers that can buy our products. At the end of the day, that's what you want from your investor, right?" Dr. Amr Awadallah, co-founder and CEO of Vectara

The world doesn't change because incumbents decide it should. It changes because someone, somewhere, decides the system is broken and has the conviction to build something better.
From AI to global commerce, from infrastructure to wealth management, from money movement to identity, from data to energy, the greatest breakthroughs come from those willing to challenge what's safe, familiar, and comfortable.
At Ribbit, we partner with these rebels. But we don't just back them, their technology or their business models. We back their ability to build brands that matter. The founders who see the cracks before anyone else and know that fixing them isn't enough. You have to make people believe in the fix.
We bring conviction, capital, and a global network. But most importantly, we bring an obsession with brand. Because the companies that reshape industries don't just solve problems. They change how people think and feel about entire categories.
We've partnered with entrepreneurs on nearly every continent who understand this truth: when you combine vision with relentless execution and the ability to build brands people love, industries don't just transform. They surrender. The status quo may be powerful, but it's rarely prepared for the right kind of rebels.
The next era won't be led by the largest or the loudest. It will be led by the boldest. Those who know that changing the world means changing minds first. If you're building to challenge the status quo and make people believe, you're already speaking our language.

# NYC's B2B seed fund for founders with enterprise ambitions
We lead pre-seed and seed rounds in conviction-driven founders, often before the rest of the market sees what they see.
Our definition of B2B keeps expanding. We're increasingly focused on compute, data centers, AI infrastructure, physical AI, and robotics. If you're building something B2B that defies traditional categories, we'd love to connect.
We started Work-Bench in 2013 with a belief that New York would become one of the best places in the world to build enterprise companies. More than a decade later, that belief has become reality - and we think the best is still ahead. 🗽
We're NYC-based and NYC-biased, and backing founders anywhere who want to win customers here.
One thing hasn't changed: a great product isn't enough. The companies that win understand their customers better than anyone else - and turn that understanding into distribution.
**We believe GTM is your moat: great products get you in the game, but customer understanding and distribution are what let you win it.**
From Day 1, we work alongside founders to build it: finding the first customers, sharpening the motion, hiring the team, and scaling from seed through exit - and beyond.

visionaries.text:
# In this era of upheaval, obsession beats playbooks, ambition beats size and conviction beats consensus. We back those who run toward the fire and follow one simple rule: connecting the top 0.1% with the top 0.1%.
We believe that rather than access to large in-house teams, what the top 0.1% of founders need is a connection to the top 0.1% of experts across adjacent industries - people who've built, scaled and broken new ground.
You go big by learning from those who have done it before you. This is where our Visionaries cadre comes in: many are our LPs, and they come to the table as mentors, early customers and collaborators.
Luminary founders: The people behind companies like UiPath, Miro, FlixBus, Lovable, n8n, Spotify, Personio, Adyen and HelloFresh, Hugging Face or DeepMind - operators who've been through the journey and are ready to help others do the same.
Industrial family entrepreneurs: Leaders of companies such as Swarovski, Mittal, Haniel, Stihl, Henkel, Siemens, Oetker, Fiege and Bitburger. Together, they represent over 90% of Europe's most influential industrial families - and give our founders a direct route to enterprise customers and unique market insights.
Join the cadre
## The Visionaries Era: Hungry beats big.
We burned the map.
We're in the middle of the fastest transformation any of us will ever witness. The old frameworks are being shredded to pieces. Anyone who tells you they know what comes next is fooling themselves.
We don't pretend to have all the answers.
What we know is this: in every era of upheaval, one thing has mattered more than any other. Not capital, thesis or strategy.
The person. The one who wakes up obsessed, works with Herculean power, and still goes to sleep unsatisfied, having yet more to offer to this world.
AI will flatten every advantage except that one.
So we're doing the one thing we know how to: We back those who run toward the fire.
And we run toward it ourselves. Every morning, we wake up with one ambition: to build the defining venture firm of this era. Not on the back of past laurels.
Because in moments of reset, the future doesn't care that much about our past.
Instead, our edge comes from the same force we look for in founders: Obsession.
Because in every generational shift:
Obsession beats playbooks.
Ambition beats size.
Conviction beats consensus.
## Hungry beats big.
We reject the institutional bloat that defines much of today's VC industry.
Multistage firms have industrialised venture, scaling VC platforms like tech companies. But no amount of scaling can take away from the fact that venture is an *outlier* business.
So we follow one very simple rule:
Connecting the top 0.1% with the top 0.1%.
The founders redefining the future deserve nothing less than those who have already built it once.

## **About Us**
Launch Africa is a leading Pan-African VC fund solving the significant funding gap in the Seed and pre-Series A investment landscape in Africa. With a decade-long track record of venture building alongside some of the smartest founding teams in Africa, we back startups across multiple sectors, regions, and products that tackle the most meaningful challenges on the continent.
#### **Building the Future of African Ventures**
Our team is comprised of passionate and experienced professionals who bring a diverse range of expertise to the table. Drawing on our collective knowledge and deep understanding of the African market combined with our unique high touch, high scale approach, we identify and back promising startups across multiple sectors and regions.
We believe in the power of entrepreneurship and innovation to transform Africa's economic landscape and create sustainable, impactful solutions.
OUR PORTFOLIO
## About Launch Africa
Launch Africa Ventures was founded by Zachariah George and Janade Du Plessis in 2020. Zach and Janade have been pioneers of early-stage venture capital in Africa since 2014, bridging the funding gap for Seed and pre-Series A startups across the African continent. Zach's investment banking and Angel investing experience together with Janade's expertise in entrepreneurship, research and banking provided the early foundation from which the broader Launch Africa team have gone on to invest, grow and scale more than 150 startups across Africa solving critical challenges across multiple sectors.
Since 2020, Launch Africa has raised just over US$36 million in its first fund, investing US$31 million into 133 startups across 22 countries, with impressive returns. They aim to convert investments into distributions and launch new funds, nurturing top-performing portfolio companies.
Their success lies in fostering strong relationships, democratizing venture capital access, and learning from global ecosystems.
Closing the funding gap is vital for innovation and growth, making Launch Africa a pivotal force in Africa's startup landscape.

The process of updating Solana has waterfall effects on Solana's incentive design, validator economics, and therefore, validator set equity. Revisiting L1 Tokens as Money: A Critique of 'Monetary Premium'
June 30, 2025
Mario Laul
One of the oldest debates in crypto focuses on the relationship between the adoption of L1 blockchain networks and the value accrual of their native tokens. The debate is unresolved but it is generally believed that, as long as the L1 token is the preferred asset for transacting on the network, the most widely adopted networks will also end up hosting the most valuable tokens. While the details of the exact argument are network- and token-specific, there is one additional idea that has been echoing in these discussions for at least 10 years. For many, it is the most important distinguishing factor between a handful of L1 'blue chips' and the evergrowing long tail of the cryptoasset universe at large. That idea is known as 'monetary premium' and it is rooted in a fundamental misunderstanding of money.

In addition to capital, we provide first-hand expertise and insights in strategy, operational execution, team-building, growth, technology, product development, networking, fundraising and more.

### FAQ
What industries do we invest in?
Technology is our core. We invest across industries, backing founders who use technology to create large new markets or fundamentally improve existing ones, building solutions for both consumers and enterprises. Our investments span financial services, healthcare, education, ecommerce, marketplaces and software, among other sectors.
We believe AI will expand and accelerate these opportunities, transforming how people interact with technology and how products are built and businesses operate. In Latin America, we see particular promise at the application layer, where founders can address local needs with better solutions and tackle previously intractable problems, and at the infrastructure layer, where the region's abundant energy resources and proximity to the United States create opportunities to support growing global demand for computing capacity.
What stages do we get involved at?
Our early-stage funds make initial investments from pre-seed and seed through Series A and Series B. We partner with founders at a wide range of starting points-from a promising idea to a business gaining traction and scaling-and aim to support them through multiple rounds as their companies grow.
Our opportunity funds invest from Series C through pre-IPO financing, extending our ability to partner with entrepreneurs throughout their journeys.
What is our geographic focus?
We mostly invest in companies that target Latin America as their main initial market.
We strongly believe in the enormous opportunity that the technology ecosystem presents in the region, and in our capacity to add significant value across Latin America, since it is an ecosystem we have been involved with for more than 20 years as entrepreneurs, mentors, and investors.
What characteristics do we look for in entrepreneurs?
We look forward to partnering with visionary and inspirational founders, who are honest, determined, and purpose driven.
Entrepreneurs that know with clarity not only what they want to accomplish, but also why they want to do it. That always see the glass half-full, relentlessly search for the light at the end of the tunnel, and challenge all boundaries to bend reality and change the world.

Five years ago, building a DEX or borrow/lend protocol meant raising $3 million, hiring five engineers, and spending six months on an MVP. Ask a frontier AI model to build a perps exchange, and you can get a matching engine, risk engine, trading interface, APIs, and most of what you need out of the box.

Today, we are announcing that Multicoin led a $4 million seed round in Birch Hill, a vertically integrated onchain credit platform that connects institutional credit supply and stablecoin-denominated demand. Credit is the oldest method of capital formation in history, and it is inherently a trust and coordination problem. # Footwork is an early-stage focused venture capital firm.
/ˈfo͝otˌwərk/
n. 1. Skillful maneuvering; an adroit response to new opportunities, to achieve a goal.
2. The manner in which one moves one's feet; the foundation for many individual and team activities such as basketball, boxing, cricket, dancing, soccer, and tennis.
## Who we are
We lead and co-lead Series A and Seed rounds, in companies with early signs of product-market fit. We typically invest between $1 and $15 million initially. We focus on consumer technology and the consumerization of enterprise technology. We're inspired by founders, and wake up every day excited to get to work with teams building the next generation of category-defining companies.
Our equal partnership combines world-class investing and operating experience. We work daily out of our office in the Dogpatch neighborhood of San Francisco.
Footwork launched in April 2021 with a $175M Fund I, and we began investing our $225M Fund II in 2025.
We've invested in 25 companies as of Q4 2026, including Table22, Cradlewise, Trendsi, Portex, Heard, Felt, Power, ReflexAI, WindBorne, Watershed, Tracksuit, Honeydew, Benable, GPTZero, Elicit, Fuse, Confido, Waldo, Snout, Protege, Anything, Monk, and several that are not yet announced.
### Mike Smith
Mike was President and COO at Stitch Fix, from idea to IPO and beyond. Mike serves on the public company boards of MillerKnoll ($MLKN), and Ulta Beauty ($ULTA). He was previously COO of Walmart.com. Mike found his footwork growing up in Northern Virginia, playing basketball and soccer.
@msmith492
### Nikhil Basu Trivedi
Nikhil was Managing Director at Shasta Ventures, where he invested in Athelas, Brigit, Canva, ClassDojo, Color Health, Frame.io, Imperfect Foods, Lattice, and The Farmer's Dog. He was previously at Insight Partners and on the founding team at Artsy. Nikhil found his footwork growing up in the UK, India, and the San Francisco Bay Area, playing cricket and tennis.

Since our founding in 1998, our focus has remained consistent: early, true partnerships with non-normal entrepreneurs building consumer brands. It's great entrepreneurs - with passion, curiosity and rigor, courage and integrity - that create iconic brands.
As a firm, we specialize in what we do best: consumer. We invest under the premise that value creation comes through identifying where consumer behavior is changing, especially before it's obvious - and we are obsessed with observing how people live, work, learn, play, eat, and stay well. Often, we look at how technology and consumer centricity are disrupting archaic industries such as real estate, health care, finance, education, food, and energy.
We seek companies that change culture and the way we live. We call it "creating a cauldron of consumer passion."
## do better than just profit
In June 2021, on the 23rd anniversary of our founding, we proudly announced our B Corp certification, joining an ever-growing list (including portfolio companies Allbirds, Lovevery, and Nécessaire). These are for-profit companies that use the power of business to build a more inclusive and sustainable economy. As investors, we partner with founders who obsess over improving the lives of consumers every single day. Additionally, a significant portion of our LP base is comprised of children's hospitals, foundations, universities, and philanthropic families who also hold this shared mission of making the world a better place. When we do well for them, the world does too.
We're excited to continue partnering with founders and investors who understand the weight of their power and who aim to shape the future - for good.
## redefining consumer
The makeup of a consumer business has drastically changed since the 90s until now, but the core remains the same: **companies that integrate into people's lives and make the world a better place.**

## What is AngelPad?
AngelPad is a seed-stage accelerator program based in NYC and San Francisco. Since 2010 we have launched more than 150 companies. Every 6 months we select about 15 teams from a huge pool of applicants (usually around 2000) to work with us. While other accelerators have decided to "scale" and take on more and more companies or launch more and more cities, we have stayed true to our original goal: **Find awesome companies with founders we like to work with and spend three very intense months with them.** This focus has paid off, we have risen to be the #1 Accelerator in the U.S. (based on a real study from MIT/Brown University) and Strictly VC called us the "Anti-Y Combinator".
During the program, we work on everything from finding product market fit, defining a target market to getting first validation for the company. We are also instrumental in helping companies prepare for fundraising and of course for investor meetings.

Icebreaker goes first. The first institutional cheque for driven founders in the New Nordics: idea stage, no traction required.
Apply for funding

## The first decisions shape everything
Your first hire. Your first customers. The product you choose to build. At the idea stage, a few decisions can change the entire company. The right customers open the door to the next hundred. The wrong ones can leave you building a product with nowhere to go.
We have been investing at this stage in the New Nordics since 2017. Our funds are small by design: the right help matters more than the biggest cheque. We typically invest €750k, with first tickets from €100k to €1.5M.
You get a team and a community of more than 500 portfolio founders and key people, a call or message away. Whatever you are working through, someone has probably been there.
Across more than 150 startup journeys, we have seen first ideas, small and big pivots, seed rounds, growth rounds and exits. Whatever comes, we don't panic.
Tell us your idea

## First in Long after
In at the start. Around for the arc.
01  First in We write the first institutional VC cheque - Seed and Pre-Series A - into a handful of founders each year. Before the deck is polished or the market has named the problem.
02  Long after Our first cheque is a beginning, not a position. We follow on through Series A, B and C - keeping the seat we earned at the start.
03  Aligned, *not just invested* Capital is the easy part. Showing up through the unfashionable quarters, the hard pivots, and the founder calls at odd hours - that is the actual job.
04  Conviction, *not coverage* The homework on the market is done before the meeting, not after. We don't reverse-engineer conviction from a charismatic deck. We are thesis-forward.
05  Lead. *Not follow* We lead the round - set terms, take the board seat, and put our name first on the cap table. If we're in, we're in deep enough to be accountable for the outcome.

We are a first-check VC fund backing Baltic founders at inception and pre-seed. We're a generalist early-stage investor with a strong focus on AI first software. We typically invest €100k to €500k as an initial check, with follow-on capacity up to €1M.

01
## How much do you invest?
Our initial ticket is €100k to €500k depending on your stage, with follow-on capacity up to €1m. We can lead rounds or co-invest with other investors.
02
## Do you invest only in Baltics?
Yes. We back founders from Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia. If you are a Baltic founder with an HQ outside of the Baltics, we want to hear from you.
03
## What do I get besides money?
Access to our platform of 100+ operators who've built and scaled before, 250+ founders in the network, and years of practical know-how. It's yours for life once you're in.
04
## Am I too early to apply?
We invest at inception and pre-seed. If you have a bold idea and the right team behind it, we want to hear from you. Nothing is too early.
05
## What is the process?
Fill in a 4-minute application form and we'll get back to you within 48 hours. From there, you'll have a call with the investment team. If we see a fit, we'll plan 2-3 additional meetings until we can make a decision. No lengthy processes, no gatekeeping.

## Paving the way for purpose driven founders
We invest in ambitious founders with groundbreaking visions for a regenerative and sustainable future.
Get started
### Build on a solid foundation
We are here to empower you along your founder journey, through investment from start to series B. We show you how to plan and strategize the next steps for your business, preparing you for fundraising and introducing you to the right co-investors.
### Streamline your vision
We won't waste your time with lecture-style presentations, but we will focus on matching you with relevant experts and mentors to support you with your most important challenges.

The success of your founder journey lies with you, but joining our global community of ambitious founders will get you on the radar of top investors and industry players, helping drive exposure for your startup at the right time and place.

# Some Call You Founders. We Call You Superheroes.
When you're on a mission, you're more than a founder. You. Are. A. Superhero.
Let's go
##
# The world's not going to change itself. Will you do it?
Ordinary life is for ordinary people. For Superheroes, the choice to lead that ordinary life is not an option. They team up with the like-minded and unite their superpowers to build something extraordinary, making ordinary life better. Are you in?
"Which will hold greater rule over you? Your fear or your curiosity?"
-Wonder Woman
##
# Seed funding for the superheroes.
In case you haven´t noticed yet, we are a VC fund. Nothing more, nothing less. So tell us who you are, why do you do this and what you look for. We initially invest up to 1M€ to help you get to the next level, and our primary focus is on software-driven startups in the New Nordics (Finland and the Baltics). We currently invest from our 2024 fund. Occasionally we might join a round outside the New Nordics too.
We want you to answer 2 simple questions:
"Why us?"
"Why now?
Everything else is nice to have. Ultimately, you matter. As simple as that.

# We invest in Nordic founders with global ambitions
We believe that the most successful companies of our time will be the ones solving real problems. The entrepreneurs that improve the way we live in a scalable way, will create long term profit as well as increase environmental and social sustainability.
We invest in exceptional early-stage tech companies founded by entrepreneurs with global ambitions. We believe that investing in a founder is a mutual partnership, and we know that building great and valuable companies takes time.
We are a Nordic venture capital firm run by experienced venture capitalists, operators and founders that helped create billion-dollar companies.
Meet the team
## The latest
14 October 2026
### Alliance VC co-led Sanna's $3.2M seed round
Sanna, an AI-native accounting firm that handles all your accounting needs at a fixed price, managed by authorised accountants, has raised a $3.2M seed round co-led by Alliance VC and Skyfall Ventures. Sondo Capital, Wave Ventures and a great set of angel investors participated in the round.
See coverage from Shifter (🇳🇴), DN ($,🇳🇴), NRK (🇳🇴) and Dealroom.
7 October 2026
### Boost AI has been acquired by Automation Anywhere
Alliance VC's portfolio company Boost AI has been acquired by Automation Anywhere. The financial terms of the transaction have not been disclosed. The transaction is expected to close in Q4 2026.
See the company announcement and the Shifter article.
29 September 2026
### General Intuition has raised $220M at a $6.2B valuation
General Intuition has raised another equity round of $220M at a $6.2B valuation from Valor Equity Partners, Atreides, 776, Point72, Khosla Ventures, and General Catalyst to make an entirely new class of foundation models available. The models are trained on billions of action-labeled videos and are capable of acting in realtime in never seen before environments.
See the company announcement and coverage by Dealroom.
23 September 2026
### Alliance VC invests in Spiich Labs €3M seed round
Spiich Labs believes sales is human and enable salespeople to focus on customers by automating prospecting, planning and data entry and many more things. Alliance VC has invested in the company's €3M seed round.
EU-Startups, TechFundingNews, Breakit ($,🇸🇪), Shifter.no (🇳🇴)

### Newcode has raised a series A
Newcode has raised a $13.5M Series A, bringing total funding since inception to $20M. OnDean Forward led the round with The LegalTech Fund, Relativity, and Antiportfolio Ventures participating. The new round brings strong legal tech domain expertise and more fuel behind the mission to deliver a configurable AI harness to the legal industry, enabling firm owned intelligence.
See company announcement and Artificial Lawyer article.

Days rather than weeks between first meeting & signed term sheet. The market may change its pace, we never do.

Deeply committed investor that aims for a 100% hit rate: no spray and pray with us, you will be 1 of the 2 companies we invest in each year.

## Google
In 1999, Andy Bechtolsheim introduced us to two Stanford graduates, Larry Page and Sergey Brin. They'd built PageRank, a superior search algorithm that overwhelmed Stanford's network with demand. Banished from campus, they needed capital and scale-fast.
Their 17-page deck had just two pages of numbers and three cartoons. As the eighteenth search engine with no business model and no team, they faced long odds. But when John Doerr asked how big Google would be, they answered: "$10 billion in revenue." We wrote our largest check ever.
The founders weren't sold on traditional management or recruiting a CEO. John connected them with Scott Cook, Bill Gates, Andy Grove, and Steve Jobs for advice. The executive search led to Eric Schmidt, an experienced tech leader from Sun Microsystems. We helped build their team with Wayne Rosing (VP Engineering) and Jonathan Rosenberg (SVP Product), introduced OKRs for goal-setting, and brought in executive coach Bill Campbell to develop leadership skills.
Our investment in Google delivered exceptional returns and transformed how the world accesses information. John continues as a board director of Alphabet, Inc.

## About
We are an independent, German venture capital firm, investing in capital-efficient, validated businesses in DACH since 2007. Across four fund generations, we have backed 60+ companies, built €400m in AuM, and delivered top-quartile returns, including 18 successful exits.
We don't chase hype. We invest in businesses in established markets with solid fundamentals, genuine customer demand, and a clear exit path, across Tech-Enabled Services, Vertical Software, and "Mittelstand" Transformation, with a focus on the DACH region. Our initial tickets range from €1m to €5m.
Our experienced team combines deep sector expertise across Consumer & Prosumer, Health & Food, and Business & Energy Efficiency with a genuinely hands-on approach. We engage closely, consistently, and stay loyal through multiple financing rounds. Founders benefit from our broad network of follow-on investors, built over two decades of active investing.
At Vorwerk Ventures, we believe the best companies are built on real demand, sound economics, and trusted partnerships, and we are proud to back the entrepreneurs making that happen.

Our portfolio is concentrated by design. Fewer investments means deeper work. Before we ever write a check, we do months of original research until we hold the sharpest perspective possible. We put our effort where it matters most, and we're relentless about closing the gap between where a company is and where it could be. Our measure of success is simple: every founder can point to the difference we made.
